revision.text: In this section we are going to build a configuration file for FPG-EYE's fpga from a source platform with binary camera. For our example we will use the platform camera_50.

In this section we are going to build a configuration file for FPG-EYE's fpga from a source platform with binary camera. For our example we will use the platform [svn+ssh://anonymous@svn.tuxfamily.org/svnroot/erika/erikae/repos/ee/trunk/ee/examples/mico32/demo/platforms/camera_50/msb/]

In this section we are going to build a configuration file for FPG-EYE's fpga from a source platform with binary camera. For our example we will use the platform [[svn+ssh://anonymous@svn.tuxfamily.org/svnroot/erika/erikae/repos/ee/trunk/ee/examples/mico32/demo/platforms/camera_50/msb/ camera_50]]
= Import platform project in MSB Ide =
After downloaded the camera_50 platform project file from svn, open the MSB Ide software. Now click on ''MSB'' button like follow figure:
[[File:select_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| ''MSB'' button]]
Now open the ''Open Platform'' form:
[[File:open_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Open ''MSB'' platform]]
Select the ''camera_50.msb'' from ''Open Platform'' dialog form:
[[File:select_camera_50_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Select ''camera_50.msb'']]
Now you can see the platform architecture like the follow figure:
[[File:platform architecture_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Select ''camera_50.msb'' platform architecture]]

revision.comment: /* Import platform project in MSB Ide */
revision.text:
In this section we are going to build a configuration file for FPG-EYE's fpga from a source platform with binary camera. For our example we will use the platform [[svn+ssh://anonymous@svn.tuxfamily.org/svnroot/erika/erikae/repos/ee/trunk/ee/examples/mico32/demo/platforms/camera_50/msb/ camera_50]]
= Import platform project in MSB Ide =
After downloaded the camera_50 platform project file from svn, open the MSB Ide software. Now click on ''MSB'' button like follow figure:
[[File:select_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| ''MSB'' button]]
Now open the ''Open Platform'' form:
[[File:open_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Open ''MSB'' platform]]
Select the ''camera_50.msb'' from ''Open Platform'' dialog form:
[[File:select_camera_50_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Select ''camera_50.msb'']]
Now you can see the platform architecture like the follow figure:
[[File:platform architecture_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Select ''camera_50.msb'' platform architecture]]
We recommend not to change the device's addresses in the platform. The last step to do is generate the platform source by clicking on the ''Run Generator'' like follow figure:
[[File:run_generator_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Clicking on ''Run Generator'' we have the platform source]]

In this section we are going to build a configuration file for FPG-EYE's fpga from a source platform with binary camera. For our example we will use the platform [[svn+ssh://anonymous@svn.tuxfamily.org/svnroot/erika/erikae/repos/ee/trunk/ee/examples/mico32/demo/platforms/camera_50/msb/ camera_50]]
= Import platform project in MSB Ide =
After downloaded the camera_50 platform project file from svn, open the MSB Ide software. Now click on ''MSB'' button like follow figure:
[[File:select_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| ''MSB'' button]]
Now open the ''Open Platform'' form:
[[File:open_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Open ''MSB'' platform]]
Select the ''camera_50.msb'' from ''Open Platform'' dialog form:
[[File:select_camera_50_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Select ''camera_50.msb'']]
Now you can see the platform architecture like the follow figure:
[[File:platform architecture_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Select ''camera_50.msb'' platform architecture]]
We recommend not to make any changes to the platform. The last step to do is generate the platform source by clicking on the ''Run Generator'' like follow figure:
[[File:run_generator_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Clicking on ''Run Generator'' we have the platform source]]
Now we have the mico32 platform in Verilog source. In the next session we will see how to compile the Verilog code for the FPGA configuration file.
= Import hardware platform project in ispLever Ide =

In this section we are going to build a configuration file for FPG-EYE's fpga from a source platform with binary camera. For our example we will use the platform [[svn+ssh://anonymous@svn.tuxfamily.org/svnroot/erika/erikae/repos/ee/trunk/ee/examples/mico32/demo/platforms/camera_50/msb/ camera_50]] You can find the MSB file project in the directory: ee/trunk/ee/examples/mico32/demo/platforms/camera_50/msb/ You can find the ispLever file project in the directory: ee/examples/mico32/demo/platforms/camera_50/isplever/
= Import platform project in MSB Ide =
After downloaded the camera_50 platform project file from svn, open the MSB Ide software. Now click on ''MSB'' button like follow figure:
[[File:select_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| ''MSB'' button]]
Now open the ''Open Platform'' form:
[[File:open_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Open ''MSB'' platform]]
Select the ''camera_50.msb'' from ''Open Platform'' dialog form:
[[File:select_camera_50_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Select ''camera_50.msb'']]
Now you can see the platform architecture like the follow figure:
[[File:platform architecture_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Select ''camera_50.msb'' platform architecture]]
We recommend not to make any changes to the platform. The last step to do is generate the platform source by clicking on the ''Run Generator'' like follow figure:
[[File:run_generator_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Clicking on ''Run Generator'' we have the platform source]]
Now we have the mico32 platform in Verilog source. In the next session we will see how to compile the Verilog code for the FPGA configuration file.
= Import hardware platform project in ispLever Ide =
Open [[http://www.latticesemi.com/products/designsoftware/isplever/isplever/index.cfm?source=sidebar ispLever Ide]]

In this section we are going to build a configuration file for FPG-EYE's fpga from a source platform with binary camera. For our example we will use the platform [[svn+ssh://anonymous@svn.tuxfamily.org/svnroot/erika/erikae/repos/ee/trunk/ee/examples/mico32/demo/platforms/camera_50/msb/ camera_50]] You can find the MSB file project in the directory: ee/trunk/ee/examples/mico32/demo/platforms/camera_50/msb/ You can find the ispLever file project in the directory: ee/examples/mico32/demo/platforms/camera_50/isplever/
= Import platform project in MSB Ide =
After downloaded the camera_50 platform project file from svn, open the MSB Ide software. Now click on ''MSB'' button like follow figure:
[[File:select_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| ''MSB'' button]]
Now open the ''Open Platform'' form:
[[File:open_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Open ''MSB'' platform]]
Select the ''camera_50.msb'' from ''Open Platform'' dialog form:
[[File:select_camera_50_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Select ''camera_50.msb'']]
Now you can see the platform architecture like the follow figure:
[[File:platform architecture_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Select ''camera_50.msb'' platform architecture]]
We recommend not to make any changes to the platform. The last step to do is generate the platform source by clicking on the ''Run Generator'' like follow figure:
[[File:run_generator_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Clicking on ''Run Generator'' we have the platform source]]
Now we have the mico32 platform in Verilog source. In the next session we will see how to compile the Verilog code for the FPGA configuration file.
= Import hardware platform project in ispLever Ide =
Open [http://www.latticesemi.com/products/designsoftware/isplever/isplever/index.cfm?source=sidebar ispLever Ide] and click on ''Open Project'' in the ''File menu'':
[[File:open_project_from_ispLever_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| ''Open project'' from ispLever]]
Now selected the ''camera_50.msb'' in your repository copy:
[[File:camera_50_from_ispLever_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| ''Open project'' from ispLever]]
The hardware project structure is now visible in the ''Sources in the Project''. Be sure than the ''Active Top Module'' is the ''camera_50_wrapper.v'' like follow figure:
[[File:struct_camera_50_from_ispLever_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| ''ispLever'' project structure]]
Before compile the ispLever project there are two steps to do. See them in the next sections.
== Importing ''camera_component_mod.ngo'' in the ispLever ==

In this section we are going to build a configuration file for FPG-EYE's fpga from a source platform with binary camera. For our example we will use the platform [[svn+ssh://anonymous@svn.tuxfamily.org/svnroot/erika/erikae/repos/ee/trunk/ee/examples/mico32/demo/platforms/camera_50/msb/ camera_50]] You can find the MSB file project in the directory: ee/trunk/ee/examples/mico32/demo/platforms/camera_50/msb/ You can find the ispLever file project in the directory: ee/examples/mico32/demo/platforms/camera_50/isplever/
= Import platform project in MSB Ide =
After downloaded the camera_50 platform project file from svn, open the MSB Ide software. Now click on ''MSB'' button like follow figure:

Now open the ''Open Platform'' form:

Select the ''camera_50.msb'' from ''Open Platform'' dialog form:

Now you can see the platform architecture like the follow figure:

We recommend not to make any changes to the platform. The last step to do is generate the platform source by clicking on the ''Run Generator'' like follow figure:
[[File:run_generator_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Clicking on ''Run Generator'' we have the platform source]]
Now we have the mico32 platform in Verilog source. In the next session we will see how to compile the Verilog code for the FPGA configuration file.
= Import hardware platform project in ispLever Ide =
Open [http://www.latticesemi.com/products/designsoftware/isplever/isplever/index.cfm?source=sidebar ispLever Ide] and click on ''Open Project'' in the ''File menu'':
[[File:open_project_from_ispLever_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| ''Open project'' from ispLever]]
Now selected the ''camera_50.msb'' in your repository copy:
[[File:camera_50_from_ispLever_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| ''Open project'' from ispLever]]
The hardware project structure is now visible in the ''Sources in the Project''. Be sure than the ''Active Top Module'' is the ''camera_50_wrapper.v'' like follow figure:
[[File:struct_camera_50_from_ispLever_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| ''ispLever'' project structure]]
Before compile the ispLever project there are two steps to do. See them in the next sections.
== Importing ''camera_component_mod.ngo'' in the ispLever ==
The component camera installed in the platform camera_50 is a binary version. So is necessary to import in the ispLever the netlist of the camera. It's possible to move the file ''camera_component_mod.ngo'', present in the [[packet camera]] in the ispLever directory project.

The [http://www.latticesemi.com/products/designsoftware/micodevelopmenttools/index.cfm ''MSB''] file project is in the directory: ''ee/trunk/ee/examples/mico32/demo/platforms/camera_50/msb/'', while the ispLever file project is in the directory: 'ee/examples/mico32/demo/platforms/camera_50/isplever/''
== Import platform project in MSB Ide ==
Open the [http://www.latticesemi.com/products/designsoftware/micodevelopmenttools/index.cfm ''MSB Ide''] software, and click on '''MSB Perspective''' button (as the following figure):
[[File:select_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| '''MSB''' button]]
Open the '''Open Platform form''' by click on the '''File->Open Platform''' menu item (as the following figure):
[[File:open_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Open '''MSB''' platform]]
After click on '''Browse''' button and find the file ''camera_50.msb'' from your repository copy:
[[File:select_camera_50_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Select ''camera_50.msb'']]
Now the platform's architecture is visible from '''Sources in Project''' window (as the following figure):
[[File:platform architecture_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Select ''camera_50.msb'' platform architecture]]
It is recommended not to make any changes to the platform. The last step to do is generate the platform source by clicking on the '''Run Generator''' menu item (as the following figure):
[[File:run_generator_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Clicking on '''Run Generator''' we have the platform source]]
So the [http://www.latticesemi.com/products/intellectualproperty/ipcores/mico32/index.cfm mico32 platform] in Verilog source is generated. For use the platform in FPG-EYE, the source code must be compiled in binary format. The next session will be how to compile the [http://www.verilog.com/ Verilog] code to FPGA configuration file.
== Import hardware platform project in ispLever Ide ==
Open [http://www.latticesemi.com/products/designsoftware/isplever/isplever/index.cfm?source=sidebar ispLever Ide] and click on ''Open Project'' in the ''File menu'':
[[File:open_project_from_ispLever_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| ''Open project'' from ispLever]]
Now select the ''camera_50.msb'' in your repository copy:
[[File:camera_50_from_ispLever_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| ''Open project'' from ispLever]]
The hardware project structure is now visible in the ''Sources in the Project''. Be sure than the ''Active Top Module'' is the ''camera_50_wrapper.v'' like follow figure:
[[File:struct_camera_50_from_ispLever_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| ''ispLever'' project structure]]
Before compile the ispLever project there are two steps to do. See them in the next sections.
=== Importing ''camera_component_mod.ngo'' in the ispLever ===
The component camera installed in the platform camera_50 is a binary version. So is necessary to import in the ispLever the netlist of the camera. It's possible to move the file ''camera_component_mod.ngo'', present in the [[packet camera]] in the ispLever project directory.
[[File:camera_component_mod_in_ispLever_directory.png|center|thumb|700px| ''camera_component_mod.ngo'' in ispLever project directory]]
=== Importing ''meminit_ebr.mem'' bootloader file in the ispLever ===
The file ''meminit_ebr.mem'' is a compiled file. It's the program bootloder than will placed in ebr non volatile memory. For the bootloder reference guide see the section: [[mico32_bootloader]]. The file is placed in the [[packet camera]]. Place it into ispLever project directory:
[[File:meminit_ebr_mem_in_ispLever_directory.png|center|thumb|700px| ''meminit_ebr.mem'' in ispLever project directory]]
== Build the platform with ispLever ==
Now is possible compile the platform. From ''Processes of current source'' click with right button mouse on voice ''Generate Data File (JEDEC)'', from menu select ''Start'' as the following figure:

[[File:meminit_ebr_mem_in_ispLever_directory.png|center|thumb|700px| ''meminit_ebr.mem'' in ispLever project directory]]

This page explains how to build a configuration file for FPG-EYE's fpga from a source platform with binary camera. To do that you neead a local copy of Erika repopsitory, to get that follow [[ERIKA Enterprise and RT-Druid SVN Access]] page's instructions. == Import platform project in LatticeMico System IDE ==
Launch [http://www.latticesemi.com/products/designsoftware/micodevelopmenttools/index.cfm ''MSB''] software, and click on '''MSB Perspective''' button (as the following figure):
[[File:select_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| '''MSB''' button]]
Open the '''Open Platform form''' by selecting the '''File->Open Platform''' menu item:
[[File:open_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Open '''MSB''' platform]]
Click the '''Browse''' button and load the file ''camera_50.msb'' from the repository copy:
[[File:select_camera_50_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Select ''camera_50.msb'']]
The platform's architecture is visible under '''Sources in Project''' window:
[[File:platform architecture_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Select ''camera_50.msb'' platform architecture]]
Note: Do not to make any changes to the platform. And finally, generate the platform source by selecting the '''Run Generator''' menu item:

[[File:open_project_from_ispLever_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| ''Open project'' from ispLever]]

[[File:meminit_ebr_mem_in_ispLever_directory.png|center|thumb|700px| ''meminit_ebr.mem'' in ispLever project directory]]

= Introduction = This page explains how to build a configuration file for FPG-EYE's fpga from a source platform with binary camera. To do that you neead a local copy of Erika repopsitory,follow [[ERIKA_Enterprise_and_RT-Druid_SVN_Access#Anonymous.2C_readonly_access | ERIKA_Enterprise_and_RT-Druid_SVN_Access]] page's instructions to get that. The [http://www.latticesemi.com/products/designsoftware/micodevelopmenttools/index.cfm LatticeMico System] file project is located in the directory: ''ee/trunk/ee/examples/mico32/demo/platforms/camera_50/msb'', while the ispLever file project is located in the directory: ''ee/examples/mico32/demo/platforms/camera_50/isplever'' inside of ERIKA Enterprise repository.
= Import platform project in LatticeMico System IDE =
Launch [http://www.latticesemi.com/products/designsoftware/micodevelopmenttools/index.cfm ''LatticeMico System''] software, and click on '''MSB Perspective''' button (as the following figure):
[[File:select_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| '''MSB''' button]]
Open the '''Open Platform form''' by selecting the '''File->Open Platform''' menu item:
[[File:open_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Open '''MSB''' platform]]
Click the '''Browse''' button and load the file ''camera_50.msb'' from the repository copy:
[[File:select_camera_50_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Select ''camera_50.msb'']]
The platform's architecture is visible under '''Sources in Project''' window:
[[File:platform architecture_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Select ''camera_50.msb'' platform architecture]]
Note: Do not to make any changes to the platform. And finally, generate the platform source by selecting the '''Run Generator''' menu item:
[[File:run_generator_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Clicking on '''Run Generator''' we have the platform source]]
The [http://www.latticesemi.com/products/intellectualproperty/ipcores/mico32/index.cfm mico32 platform] Verilog source is generated. To use the platform in FPG-EYE, the source code must be compiled in binary format. The next session explain about how to compile the [http://www.verilog.com/ Verilog] code for FPGA configuration file.
= Import hardware platform project in ispLever Ide =
Open [http://www.latticesemi.com/products/designsoftware/isplever/isplever/index.cfm?source=sidebar ispLever Ide] and select ''Open Project'' under ''File menu'':
[[File:open_project_from_ispLever_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| ''Open project'' from ispLever]]
Load ''camera_50.msb'' from the repository copy:
[[File:camera_50_from_ispLever_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Load ''camera_50.msb'']]
The hardware project structure is visible under ''Sources in the Project'' window. Ensure that ''camera_50_wrapper.v'' is selected and active:
[[File:struct_camera_50_from_ispLever_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| ''ispLever'' project structure]]
Before compiling the ispLever project, there are two more steps to perform (refer sections below).
== Importing ''camera_component_mod.ngo'' in the ispLever ==
The component camera installed in the platform camera_50 is a binary version. So it is necessary to import in the ispLever the netlist of the camera. To do this, move the file ''camera_component_mod.ngo'', from the [[packet camera]] to the ispLever project directory.
[[File:camera_component_mod_in_ispLever_directory.png|center|thumb|700px| ''camera_component_mod.ngo'' in ispLever project directory]]
== Importing ''meminit_ebr.mem'' bootloader file in the ispLever ==
The file ''meminit_ebr.mem'' is a compiled file. It is the program bootloader which would be placed in the ebr non volatile memory. For the bootloader reference guide, refer section [[mico32_bootloader]]. Move this file from the [[packet camera]] to the ispLever project directory.
[[File:meminit_ebr_mem_in_ispLever_directory.png|center|thumb|700px| ''meminit_ebr.mem'' in ispLever project directory]]
= Build the platform with ispLever =
On '''Processes of current source''' click and select '''Generate Data File (JEDEC)''' then right click and select '''Force''' :
[[File:force_form_ispLever.png|center|thumb|700px| '''Force''' from '''Generate Data File (JEDEC)''' menu]]

[[File:generate_data_file_jedec_from_isplever.png|center|thumb|700px| '''Generate Data File (JEDEC)''']]

[[File:meminit_ebr_mem_in_ispLever_directory.png|center|thumb|700px| ''meminit_ebr.mem'' in ispLever project directory]]

[[File:force_form_ispLever.png|center|thumb|700px| '''Force''' from '''Generate Data File (JEDEC)''' menu]]

[[File:open_project_from_ispLever_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| ''Open project'' from ispLever]]
Load '''ee/examples/mico32/demo/platforms/camera_debug_50/isplever/camera_debug_50.syn''' inside Erika repository local copy:
[[File:camera_50_from_ispLever_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Load ''camera_50.msb'']]
The hardware project structure is visible under ''Sources in Project'' window. Ensure that ''camera_50_wrapper.v'' is selected and active:
[[File:struct_camera_50_from_ispLever_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| ''ispLever'' project structure]]
Before compiling the ispLever project, there are two more steps to perform (refer sections below).

The component camera installed in the platform camera_50 is a binary version. So it is necessary to import in the ispLever the netlist of the camera. To do this, copy the file ''camera_component_mod.ngo'', from the [[FPG-EYE Software Packet]] to the ispLever project directory.
[[File:camera_component_mod_in_ispLever_directory.png|center|thumb|700px| ''camera_component_mod.ngo'' in ispLever project directory]]

The file ''meminit_ebr.mem'' is a compiled file. It is the program bootloader which will be placed in the XP2 EBR non volatile memory. For the bootloader reference guide, refer section [[mico32_bootloader]]. Copy this file from the [[FPG-EYE Software Packet]] to the ispLever project directory.
[[File:meminit_ebr_mem_in_ispLever_directory.png|center|thumb|700px| ''meminit_ebr.mem'' in ispLever project directory]]
= Build the platform with ispLever =
On '''Processes of current source''' click and select '''Generate Data File (JEDEC)''' then right click and select '''Force''' :
[[File:force_form_ispLever.png|center|thumb|700px| '''Force''' from '''Generate Data File (JEDEC)''' menu]]
When the process is complete the file the FPGA configuration file '''JEDEC''' is ready to use.
[[File:generate_data_file_jedec_from_isplever.png|center|thumb|700px| '''Generate Data File (JEDEC)''']]
= Programming the platform on FPG-EYE board = The last step is download the '''JEDEC''' file into ''FPG-EYE''. Please follow the [[Programming the FPG-EYE board]] istructions.

Note: You don't need to make any changes to the platform. And finally, generate the platform source by selecting the '''Run Generator''' menu item:
[[File:run_generator_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Clicking on '''Run Generator''' we have the platform source]]
The [http://www.latticesemi.com/products/intellectualproperty/ipcores/mico32/index.cfm mico32] platform's Verilog source is generated. To use this platform in FPG-EYE, the source code must be compiled in binary format. The next session explains how to compile the [http://www.verilog.com/ Verilog] platform's code with ispLEVER tool.
= Import hardware platform project in ispLever IDE =
Open [http://www.latticesemi.com/products/designsoftware/isplever/isplever/index.cfm?source=sidebar ispLEVER] and select ''Open Project'' under ''File menu'':
[[File:open_project_from_ispLever_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| ''Open project'' from ispLever]]
Load '''ee/examples/mico32/demo/platforms/camera_debug_50/isplever/camera_debug_50.syn''' inside Erika repository local copy:
[[File:camera_50_from_ispLever_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Load ''camera_50.msb'']]
The hardware project structure is visible under ''Sources in Project'' window. Ensure that ''camera_50_wrapper.v'' is selected and active:
[[File:struct_camera_50_from_ispLever_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| ''ispLever'' project structure]]
Before compiling the ispLever project, there are two more steps to perform (refer sections below).
== Importing ''camera_component_mod.ngo'' in the ispLever ==
The component camera installed in the platform camera_50 is a binary version. So it is necessary to import in the ispLever the netlist of the camera. To do this, copy the file ''camera_component_mod.ngo'', from the [http://download.tuxfamily.org/erika/webdownload/fpg-eye/FPG-EYE_software_packet.zip FPG-EYE Software Packet] to the ispLever project directory.
[[File:camera_component_mod_in_ispLever_directory.png|center|thumb|700px| ''camera_component_mod.ngo'' in ispLever project directory]]
== Importing ''meminit_ebr.mem'' bootloader file in the ispLEVER ==
The file ''meminit_ebr.mem'' is a compiled file. It is the program bootloader which will be placed in the XP2 EBR non volatile memory. For the bootloader reference guide, refer section [[mico32_bootloader]]. Copy this file from the [http://download.tuxfamily.org/erika/webdownload/fpg-eye/FPG-EYE_software_packet.zip FPG-EYE Software Packet] to the ispLever project directory.
[[File:meminit_ebr_mem_in_ispLever_directory.png|center|thumb|700px| ''meminit_ebr.mem'' in ispLever project directory]]
= Build the platform with ispLEVER =
On '''Processes of current source''' click and select '''Generate Data File (JEDEC)''' then right click and select '''Force''' :
[[File:force_form_ispLever.png|center|thumb|700px| '''Force''' from '''Generate Data File (JEDEC)''' menu]]
When the process is complete the file the FPGA configuration file '''JEDEC''' is ready to use.
[[File:generate_data_file_jedec_from_isplever.png|center|thumb|700px| '''Generate Data File (JEDEC)''']]
= Programming the platform on FPG-EYE board = The last step is download the '''JEDEC''' file into ''FPG-EYE''. Please follow the [[Programming the FPG-EYE board]] istructions.

= Introduction = This page explains how to build a configuration file for FPG-EYE's fpga from a source platform with binary camera. To do that you need to [[Installation of Mico32/FPG-EYE development environment | install Mico32/FPG-EYE development environment]] and a local copy of Erika repopsitory, follow [[ERIKA_Enterprise_and_RT-Druid_SVN_Access#Anonymous.2C_readonly_access | ERIKA_Enterprise_and_RT-Druid_SVN_Access]] page's instructions to get that.
= Import platform project in LatticeMico System IDE =
Launch [http://www.latticesemi.com/products/designsoftware/micodevelopmenttools/index.cfm ''LatticeMico System''] software, and click on '''MSB Perspective''' button (as the following figure):
[[File:select_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| '''MSB''' button]]
Open the '''Open Platform form''' by selecting the '''File->Open Platform''' menu item:
[[File:open_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Open '''MSB''' platform]]
Click the '''Browse''' button and load '''ee/trunk/ee/examples/mico32/demo/platforms/fpg_eye_mico32/msb/soc/fpg_eye_mico32.msb''' file inside Erika repository local copy:
[[File:Select_fpg_eye_mico32_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Select ''fpg_eye_mico32.msb'']]
The platform's architecture is visible under '''Sources in Project''' window:
[[File:fpg_eya_mico32_from_msb.png|center|thumb|700px| Select ''fpg_eye_mico32.msb'' platform architecture]]
Note: You don't need to make any changes to the platform. And finally, generate the platform source by selecting the '''Run Generator''' menu item:
[[File:fpg_eya_mico32_from_msb_run.png|center|thumb|700px| Clicking on '''Run Generator''' we have the platform source]]
The [http://www.latticesemi.com/products/intellectualproperty/ipcores/mico32/index.cfm mico32] platform's Verilog source is generated. To use this platform in FPG-EYE, the source code must be compiled in binary format. The next session explains how to compile the [http://www.verilog.com/ Verilog] platform's code with ispLEVER tool.
= Import hardware platform project in ispLever IDE =
Open [http://www.latticesemi.com/products/designsoftware/isplever/isplever/index.cfm?source=sidebar ispLEVER] and select ''Open Project'' under ''File menu'':
[[File:open_project_from_ispLever_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| ''Open project'' from ispLever]]
Load '''ee/examples/mico32/demo/platforms/fpg_eye_mico32/isplever/fpg_eye_mico32.syn''' inside Erika repository local copy:
[[File:fpg_eya_mico32_from_ispLever.png|center|thumb|700px| Load ''camera_50.msb'']]
The hardware project structure is visible under ''Sources in Project'' window. Ensure that ''camera_50_wrapper.v'' is selected and active:
[[File:struct_camera_50_from_ispLever_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| ''ispLever'' project structure]]
Before compiling the ispLever project, there are two more steps to perform (refer sections below).
== Importing ''camera_component_mod.ngo'' in the ispLever ==
The component camera installed in the platform camera_50 is a binary version. So it is necessary to import in the ispLever the netlist of the camera. To do this, copy the file ''camera_component_mod.ngo'', from the [http://download.tuxfamily.org/erika/webdownload/fpg-eye/FPG-EYE_software_packet.zip FPG-EYE Software Packet] to the ispLever project directory.
[[File:camera_component_mod_in_ispLever_directory.png|center|thumb|700px| ''camera_component_mod.ngo'' in ispLever project directory]]

For the bootloader reference guide, refer section [[mico32_bootloader]]. Copy this file from the [http://download.tuxfamily.org/erika/webdownload/fpg-eye/FPG-EYE_software_packet.zip FPG-EYE Software Packet] to the ispLever project directory.
[[File:meminit_ebr_mem_in_ispLever_directory.png|center|thumb|700px| ''meminit_ebr.mem'' in ispLever project directory]]

Launch [http://www.latticesemi.com/products/designsoftware/micodevelopmenttools/index.cfm ''LatticeMico System''] software, and click on '''MSB Perspective''' button (as the following figure):
[[File:select_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| '''MSB''' button]]
Open the '''Open Platform form''' by selecting the '''File->Open Platform''' menu item:
[[File:open_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Open '''MSB''' platform]]
Click the '''Browse''' button and load '''ee/trunk/ee/examples/mico32/demo/platforms/fpg_eye_mico32/msb/soc/fpg_eye_mico32.msb''' file inside Erika repository local copy:
[[File:Select_fpg_eye_mico32_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Select ''fpg_eye_mico32.msb'']]
The platform's architecture is visible under '''Sources in Project''' window:
[[File:fpg_eya_mico32_from_msb.png|center|thumb|700px| Select ''fpg_eye_mico32.msb'' platform architecture]]
Note: You don't need to make any changes to the platform. And finally, generate the platform source by selecting the '''Run Generator''' menu item:
[[File:fpg_eya_mico32_from_msb_run.png|center|thumb|700px| Clicking on '''Run Generator''' we have the platform source]]
The [http://www.latticesemi.com/products/intellectualproperty/ipcores/mico32/index.cfm mico32] platform's Verilog source is generated. To use this platform in FPG-EYE, the source code must be compiled in binary format. The next session explains how to compile the [http://www.verilog.com/ Verilog] platform's code with ispLEVER tool.
= Import hardware platform project in ispLever IDE =
Open [http://www.latticesemi.com/products/designsoftware/isplever/isplever/index.cfm?source=sidebar ispLEVER] and select ''Open Project'' under ''File menu'':
[[File:open_project_from_ispLever_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| ''Open project'' from ispLever]]
Load '''ee/examples/mico32/demo/platforms/fpg_eye_mico32/isplever/fpg_eye_mico32.syn''' inside Erika repository local copy:
[[File:fpg_eya_mico32_from_ispLever.png|center|thumb|700px| Load ''fpg_eye_mico32.msb'']]
The hardware project structure is visible under ''Sources in Project'' window. Ensure that ''fpg_eye_mico32_wrapper.v'' is selected and active:
[[File:fpg_eye_mico32_wrapper_active.png|center|thumb|700px| ''ispLever'' project structure]]
Before compiling the ispLever project, there are two more steps to perform (refer sections below).
== Importing ''camera_component_mod.ngo'' in the ispLever ==
The component camera installed in the platform fpg_eye_mico32 is a binary version. So it is necessary to import in the ispLever the netlist of the camera. To do this, copy the file ''camera_component_mod.ngo'', from the [http://download.tuxfamily.org/erika/webdownload/fpg-eye/FPG-EYE_software_packet.zip FPG-EYE Software Packet] to the ispLever project directory.
[[File:camera_component_ngo_in ispLever.png|center|thumb|700px| ''camera_component_mod.ngo'' in ispLever project directory]]
== Importing ''meminit_ebr.mem'' bootloader file in the ispLEVER ==
The file ''meminit_ebr.mem'' is a compiled file. It is the program bootloader which will be placed in the XP2 EBR non volatile memory. For the bootloader reference guide, refer section [[Program the flash with send_prog.py bootloader script]]. Copy this file from the [http://download.tuxfamily.org/erika/webdownload/fpg-eye/FPG-EYE_software_packet.zip FPG-EYE Software Packet] to the ispLever project directory.
[[File:isp_lever_mem_file.png|center|thumb|700px| ''meminit_ebr.mem'' in ispLever project directory]]
= Build the platform with ispLEVER =
On '''Processes of current source''' click and select '''Generate Data File (JEDEC)''' then right click and select '''Force''' :
[[File:force_form_ispLever.png|center|thumb|700px| '''Force''' from '''Generate Data File (JEDEC)''' menu]]
When the process is complete the file the FPGA configuration file '''JEDEC''' is ready to use.
[[File:generate_data_file_jedec_from_isplever.png|center|thumb|700px| '''Generate Data File (JEDEC)''']]
= Programming the platform on FPG-EYE board = The last step is download the '''JEDEC''' file into ''FPG-EYE''. Please follow the [[Programming the FPG-EYE board]] istructions.

[[File:open_project_from_ispLever_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| ''Open project'' from ispLever]]
Load '''ee/examples/mico32/demo/platforms/fpg_eye_mico32/isplever/fpg_eye_mico32.syn''' inside Erika repository local copy:
[[File:fpg_eya_mico32_from_ispLever.png|center|thumb|700px| Load ''fpg_eye_mico32.msb'']]

[[File:fpg_eye_mico32_wrapper_active.png|center|thumb|700px| ''ispLever'' project structure]]

The file ''meminit_ebr.mem'' is a compiled file. It is the program bootloader which will be placed in the XP2 EBR non volatile memory. [[File:generate_data_file_jedec_from_isplever.png|center|thumb|700px| '''Generate Data File (JEDEC)''']]

Launch [http://www.latticesemi.com/products/designsoftware/micodevelopmenttools/index.cfm ''LatticeMico System''] software, and click on '''MSB Perspective''' button (as the following figure):
[[File:select_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| '''MSB''' button]]
Open the '''Open Platform form''' by selecting the '''File->Open Platform''' menu item:
[[File:open_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Open '''MSB''' platform]]
Click the '''Browse''' button and load '''ee/trunk/ee/examples/mico32/demo/platforms/fpg_eye_mico32/msb/soc/fpg_eye_mico32.msb''' file inside Erika repository local copy:
[[File:Select_fpg_eye_mico32_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Select ''fpg_eye_mico32.msb'']]
The platform's architecture is visible under '''Sources in Project''' window:
[[File:fpg_eya_mico32_from_msb.png|center|thumb|700px| Select ''fpg_eye_mico32.msb'' platform architecture]]
Note: You don't need to make any changes to the platform. And finally, generate the platform source by selecting the '''Run Generator''' menu item:
[[File:fpg_eya_mico32_from_msb_run.png|center|thumb|700px| Clicking on '''Run Generator''' we have the platform source]]
The [http://www.latticesemi.com/products/intellectualproperty/ipcores/mico32/index.cfm mico32] platform's Verilog source is generated. To use this platform in FPG-EYE, the source code must be compiled in binary format. The next session explains how to compile the [http://www.verilog.com/ Verilog] platform's code with ispLEVER tool.
= Import hardware platform project in ispLever IDE =
Open [http://www.latticesemi.com/products/designsoftware/isplever/isplever/index.cfm?source=sidebar ispLEVER] and select ''Open Project'' under ''File menu'':
[[File:open_project_from_ispLever_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| ''Open project'' from ispLever]]
Load '''ee/examples/mico32/demo/platforms/fpg_eye_mico32/isplever/fpg_eye_mico32.syn''' inside Erika repository local copy:
[[File:fpg_eya_mico32_from_ispLever.png|center|thumb|700px| Load ''fpg_eye_mico32.msb'']]
The hardware project structure is visible under ''Sources in Project'' window. Ensure that ''fpg_eye_mico32_wrapper.v'' is selected and active:
[[File:fpg_eye_mico32_wrapper_active.png|center|thumb|700px| ''ispLever'' project structure]]
Before compiling the ispLever project, there are two more steps to perform (refer sections below).
== Importing ''camera_component_mod.ngo'' in the ispLever ==
The component camera installed in the platform ''fpg_eye_mico32'' is a binary version. So it is necessary to import in the ispLever the netlist of the camera. To do this, copy the file ''camera_component_mod.ngo'', from the [http://download.tuxfamily.org/erika/webdownload/fpg-eye/FPG-EYE_software_packet.zip FPG-EYE Software Packet] to the ispLever project directory.
[[File:camera_component_ngo_in ispLever.png|center|thumb|700px| ''camera_component_mod.ngo'' in ispLever project directory]]
== Importing ''meminit_ebr.mem'' bootloader file in the ispLEVER ==
The file ''meminit_ebr.mem'' is a compiled file. It is the program bootloader which will be placed in the XP2 EBR non volatile memory. For the bootloader reference guide, refer section [[Tutorial: Running ERIKA on Mico32 and FPG-EYE]]. Copy this file from the [http://download.tuxfamily.org/erika/webdownload/fpg-eye/FPG-EYE_software_packet.zip FPG-EYE Software Packet] to the ispLever project directory.
[[File:isp_lever_mem_file.png|center|thumb|700px| ''meminit_ebr.mem'' in ispLever project directory]]

On '''Processes of current source''' click and select '''Generate Data File (JEDEC)''' then right click and select '''Force''' :
[[File:isp_lever_compile_fpg_eye_mico32.png|center|thumb|700px| '''Force''' from '''Generate Data File (JEDEC)''' menu]]
When the process is complete the file the FPGA configuration file '''JEDEC''' is ready to use.
[[File:generate_data_file_jedec_from_isplever.png|center|thumb|700px| '''Generate Data File (JEDEC)''']]

= Introduction = This page explains how to build a configuration file for FPG-EYE's fpga from a source platform with binary camera. To do that you need to [[Installation of Mico32/FPG-EYE development environment | install Mico32/FPG-EYE development environment]] and a local copy of Erika repopsitory, follow [[ERIKA_Enterprise_and_RT-Druid_SVN_Access#Anonymous.2C_readonly_access | ERIKA_Enterprise_and_RT-Druid_SVN_Access]] page's instructions to get that.
= Import platform project in LatticeMico System IDE =
Launch [http://www.latticesemi.com/products/designsoftware/micodevelopmenttools/index.cfm ''LatticeMico System''] software, and click on '''MSB Perspective''' button (as the following figure):
[[File:select_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| '''MSB''' button]]
Open the '''Open Platform form''' by selecting the '''File->Open Platform''' menu item:
[[File:open_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Open '''MSB''' platform]]
Click the '''Browse''' button and load '''ee/trunk/ee/examples/mico32/demo/platforms/fpg_eye_mico32/msb/soc/fpg_eye_mico32.msb''' file inside Erika repository local copy:
[[File:Select_fpg_eye_mico32_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Select ''fpg_eye_mico32.msb'']]
The platform's architecture is visible under '''Sources in Project''' window:
[[File:fpg_eya_mico32_from_msb.png|center|thumb|700px| Select ''fpg_eye_mico32.msb'' platform architecture]]
Note: You don't need to make any changes to the platform. And finally, generate the platform source by selecting the '''Run Generator''' menu item:
[[File:fpg_eya_mico32_from_msb_run.png|center|thumb|700px| Clicking on '''Run Generator''' we have the platform source]]
The [http://www.latticesemi.com/products/intellectualproperty/ipcores/mico32/index.cfm mico32] platform's Verilog source is generated. To use this platform in FPG-EYE, the source code must be compiled in binary format. The next session explains how to compile the [http://www.verilog.com/ Verilog] platform's code with ispLEVER tool.

[[File:open_project_from_ispLever_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| ''Open project'' from ispLever]]

revision.text:
= Introduction = This page explains how to build a configuration file for FPG-EYE's fpga from a source platform with binary camera. Prerequisites: * [[Installation of Mico32/FPG-EYE development environment | Install Mico32/FPG-EYE development environment]] * Get a local copy of Erika repository to have the platform projects. For further info see this page:[[ERIKA_Enterprise_and_RT-Druid_SVN_Access#Anonymous.2C_readonly_access | ERIKA Enterprise and RT-Druid SVN Access instructions]]. * To download the platform JEDEC file, you need a '''programming cable''' connected to the JTAG port of the board, follow the instructions on [http://erika.tuxfamily.org/wiki/index.php?title=Programming_the_FPG-EYE_board How programming the FPG-EYE board].
= Import platform project in LatticeMico System IDE =
Launch [http://www.latticesemi.com/products/designsoftware/micodevelopmenttools/index.cfm ''LatticeMico System''] software, and click on '''MSB Perspective''' button (as the following figure):
[[File:select_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| '''MSB''' button]]
Open the '''Open Platform form''' by selecting the '''File->Open Platform''' menu item:
[[File:open_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Open '''MSB''' platform]]
Now if you are using the software ispLever click the '''Browse''' button and load '''ee/trunk/ee/examples/mico32/demo/platforms/fpg_eye_isplever/msb/soc/fpg_eye_mico32.msb''' file inside Erika repository local copy, while, if you are using the software Diamond click the '''Browse''' button and load '''ee/trunk/ee/examples/mico32/demo/platforms/fpg_eye_diamond/msb/soc/fpg_eye_mico32.msb''' file inside Erika repository local copy.
[[File:Select_fpg_eye_mico32_msb_from_msb_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| Select ''fpg_eye_mico32.msb'']]
The platform's architecture is visible under '''Sources in Project''' window:
[[File:fpg_eya_mico32_from_msb.png|center|thumb|700px| Select ''fpg_eye_mico32.msb'' platform architecture]]
Note: You don't need to make any changes to the platform. And finally, generate the platform source by selecting the '''Run Generator''' menu item:
[[File:fpg_eya_mico32_from_msb_run.png|center|thumb|700px| Clicking on '''Run Generator''' we have the platform source]]
The [http://www.latticesemi.com/products/intellectualproperty/ipcores/mico32/index.cfm mico32] platform's Verilog source is generated. To use this platform in FPG-EYE, the source code must be compiled in binary format. The next session explains how to compile the [http://www.verilog.com/ Verilog] platform's code with ispLEVER tool.
= Import hardware platform project in ispLever IDE =
Open [http://www.latticesemi.com/products/designsoftware/isplever/isplever/index.cfm?source=sidebar ispLEVER] and select ''Open Project'' under ''File menu'':
[[File:open_project_from_ispLever_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| ''Open project'' from ispLever]]
Load '''ee/examples/mico32/demo/platforms/fpg_eye_mico32/isplever/fpg_eye_mico32.syn''' inside Erika repository local copy:
[[File:fpg_eya_mico32_from_ispLever.png|center|thumb|700px| Load ''fpg_eye_mico32.msb'']]
The hardware project structure is visible under ''Sources in Project'' window. Ensure that ''fpg_eye_mico32_wrapper.v'' is selected and active:
[[File:fpg_eye_mico32_wrapper_active.png|center|thumb|700px| ''ispLever'' project structure]]
Before compiling the ispLever project, there are two more steps to perform (refer sections below).
== Importing ''camera_component_mod.ngo'' in the ispLever ==
The component camera installed in the platform ''fpg_eye_mico32'' is a binary version. So it is necessary to import in the ispLever the netlist of the camera. To do this, copy the file ''camera_component_mod.ngo'', from the [http://download.tuxfamily.org/erika/webdownload/fpg-eye/FPG-EYE_software_packet.zip FPG-EYE Software Packet] to the ispLever project directory.
[[File:camera_component_ngo_in ispLever.png|center|thumb|700px| ''camera_component_mod.ngo'' in ispLever project directory]]
== Importing ''meminit_ebr.mem'' bootloader file in the ispLEVER ==
The file ''meminit_ebr.mem'' is a compiled file. It is the program bootloader which will be placed in the XP2 EBR non volatile memory. For the bootloader reference guide, refer section [[Tutorial: Running ERIKA on Mico32 and FPG-EYE]]. Copy this file from the [http://download.tuxfamily.org/erika/webdownload/fpg-eye/FPG-EYE_software_packet.zip FPG-EYE Software Packet] to the ispLever project directory.
[[File:isp_lever_mem_file.png|center|thumb|700px| ''meminit_ebr.mem'' in ispLever project directory]]
== Build the platform with ispLEVER ==
On '''Processes of current source''' click and select '''Generate Data File (JEDEC)''' then right click and select '''Force''' :
[[File:isp_lever_compile_fpg_eye_mico32.png|center|thumb|700px| '''Force''' from '''Generate Data File (JEDEC)''' menu]]
When the process is complete the file the FPGA configuration file '''JEDEC''' is ready to use.
[[File:generate_data_file_jedec_from_isplever.png|center|thumb|700px| '''Generate Data File (JEDEC)''']]
= Import hardware platform project in Diamond IDE =
Open [http://www.latticesemi.com/products/designsoftware/diamond Diamond] and select ''Open Project'' under ''File menu'':
[[File:open_project_from_diamond_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| ''Open project'' from Diamond]]
Load '''ee/examples/mico32/demo/platforms/fpg_eye_mico32/diamond/fpg_eye_mico32.syn''' inside Erika repository local copy:
[[File:fpg_eya_mico32_from_diamond.png|center|thumb|700px| Load ''fpg_eye_mico32.msb'']]
The hardware project structure is visible under ''Sources in Project'' window. Ensure that ''fpg_eye_mico32_wrapper.v'' is selected and active:
[[File:fpg_eye_mico32_wrapper_active_diamond.png|center|thumb|700px| ''Diamond'' project structure]]
Before compiling the Diamond project, there are two more steps to perform (refer sections below).
== Importing ''camera_component_mod.ngo'' in the Diamond ==
The component camera installed in the platform ''fpg_eye_mico32'' is a binary version. So it is necessary to import in the Diamond the netlist of the camera. To do this, copy the file ''camera_component_mod.ngo'', from the [http://download.tuxfamily.org/erika/webdownload/fpg-eye/FPG-EYE_software_packet.zip FPG-EYE Software Packet] to the Diamond project directory.
[[File:camera_component_ngo_in_diamond.png|center|thumb|700px| ''camera_component_mod.ngo'' in Diamond project directory]]
== Importing ''meminit_ebr.mem'' bootloader file in the Diamond ==
The file ''meminit_ebr.mem'' is a compiled file. It is the program bootloader which will be placed in the XP2 EBR non volatile memory. For the bootloader reference guide, refer section [[Tutorial: Running ERIKA on Mico32 and FPG-EYE]]. Copy this file from the [http://download.tuxfamily.org/erika/webdownload/fpg-eye/FPG-EYE_software_packet.zip FPG-EYE Software Packet] to the Diamond project directory.
[[File:diamond_mem_file.png|center|thumb|700px| ''meminit_ebr.mem'' in Diamond project directory]]
== Build the platform with Diamond ==
On '''Processes of current source''' click and select '''Generate Data File (JEDEC)''' then right click and select '''Return All''' :
[[File:diamond_compile_fpg_eye_mico32.png|center|thumb|700px| '''Force''' from '''Generate Data File (JEDEC)''' menu]]
When the process is complete the file the FPGA configuration file '''JEDEC''' is ready to use.
[[File:generate_data_file_jedec_from_diamond.png|center|thumb|700px| '''Generate Data File (JEDEC)''']]
= Programming the platform on FPG-EYE board = The last step is download the '''JEDEC''' file into ''FPG-EYE''. Please follow the [[Programming the FPG-EYE board]] istructions.

Note: You don't need to make any changes to the platform. And finally, generate the platform source by selecting the '''Run Generator''' menu item:
[[File:fpg_eya_mico32_from_msb_run.png|center|thumb|700px| Clicking on '''Run Generator''' we have the platform source]]
The [http://www.latticesemi.com/products/intellectualproperty/ipcores/mico32/index.cfm mico32] platform's Verilog source is generated. To use this platform in FPG-EYE, the source code must be compiled in binary format. The next session explains how to compile the [http://www.verilog.com/ Verilog] platform's code with ispLEVER tool.
= Import hardware platform project in ispLever IDE =
Open [http://www.latticesemi.com/products/designsoftware/isplever/isplever/index.cfm?source=sidebar ispLEVER] and select ''Open Project'' under ''File menu'':
[[File:open_project_from_ispLever_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| ''Open project'' from ispLever]]
Load '''ee/examples/mico32/demo/platforms/fpg_eye_isplever/isplever/fpg_eye_mico32.syn''' inside Erika repository local copy:
[[File:fpg_eya_mico32_from_ispLever.png|center|thumb|700px| Load ''fpg_eye_mico32.msb'']]
The hardware project structure is visible under ''Sources in Project'' window. Ensure that ''fpg_eye_mico32_wrapper.v'' is selected and active:
[[File:fpg_eye_mico32_wrapper_active.png|center|thumb|700px| ''ispLever'' project structure]]
Before compiling the ispLever project, there are two more steps to perform (refer sections below).
== Importing ''camera_component_mod.ngo'' in the ispLever ==
The component camera installed in the platform ''fpg_eye_mico32'' is a binary version. So it is necessary to import in the ispLever the netlist of the camera. To do this, copy the file ''camera_component_mod.ngo'', from the [http://download.tuxfamily.org/erika/webdownload/fpg-eye/FPG-EYE_software_packet.zip FPG-EYE Software Packet] to the ispLever project directory.
[[File:camera_component_ngo_in ispLever.png|center|thumb|700px| ''camera_component_mod.ngo'' in ispLever project directory]]
== ''meminit_ebr.mem'' bootloader file in the ispLEVER ==
The file ''meminit_ebr.mem'' is the compiled file. It is the program bootloader which will be placed in the XP2 EBR non volatile memory. For the bootloader reference guide, refer section [[Tutorial: Running ERIKA on Mico32 and FPG-EYE]]. Be sure that the file is present in the ispLever project directory.
[[File:isp_lever_mem_file.png|center|thumb|700px| ''meminit_ebr.mem'' in ispLever project directory]]
== Build the platform with ispLEVER ==
On '''Processes of current source''' click and select '''Generate Data File (JEDEC)''' then right click and select '''Force''' :
[[File:isp_lever_compile_fpg_eye_mico32.png|center|thumb|700px| '''Force''' from '''Generate Data File (JEDEC)''' menu]]
When the process is complete the file the FPGA configuration file '''JEDEC''' is ready to use.
[[File:generate_data_file_jedec_from_isplever.png|center|thumb|700px| '''Generate Data File (JEDEC)''']]
= Import hardware platform project in Diamond IDE =
Open [http://www.latticesemi.com/products/designsoftware/diamond Diamond] and select ''Open Project'' under ''File menu'':
[[File:open_project_from_diamond_ide.png|center|thumb|700px| ''Open project'' from Diamond]]
Load '''ee/examples/mico32/demo/platforms/fpg_eye_mico32/diamond/fpg_eye_mico32.syn''' inside Erika repository local copy:
[[File:fpg_eya_mico32_from_diamond.png|center|thumb|700px| Load ''fpg_eye_mico32.msb'']]
The hardware project structure is visible under ''Sources in Project'' window. Ensure that ''fpg_eye_mico32_wrapper.v'' is selected and active:
[[File:fpg_eye_mico32_wrapper_active_diamond.png|center|thumb|700px| ''Diamond'' project structure]]
Before compiling the Diamond project, there are two more steps to perform (refer sections below).
== Importing ''camera_component_mod.ngo'' in the Diamond ==
The component camera installed in the platform ''fpg_eye_mico32'' is a binary version. So it is necessary to import in the Diamond the netlist of the camera. To do this, copy the file ''camera_component_mod.ngo'', from the [http://download.tuxfamily.org/erika/webdownload/fpg-eye/FPG-EYE_software_packet.zip FPG-EYE Software Packet] to the Diamond project directory.
[[File:camera_component_ngo_in_diamond.png|center|thumb|700px| ''camera_component_mod.ngo'' in Diamond project directory]]
== Importing ''meminit_ebr.mem'' bootloader file in the Diamond ==
The file ''meminit_ebr.mem'' is a compiled file. It is the program bootloader which will be placed in the XP2 EBR non volatile memory. For the bootloader reference guide, refer section [[Tutorial: Running ERIKA on Mico32 and FPG-EYE]]. Copy this file from the [http://download.tuxfamily.org/erika/webdownload/fpg-eye/FPG-EYE_software_packet.zip FPG-EYE Software Packet] to the Diamond project directory.
[[File:diamond_mem_file.png|center|thumb|700px| ''meminit_ebr.mem'' in Diamond project directory]]
== Build the platform with Diamond ==
On '''Processes of current source''' click and select '''Generate Data File (JEDEC)''' then right click and select '''Return All''' :
[[File:diamond_compile_fpg_eye_mico32.png|center|thumb|700px| '''Force''' from '''Generate Data File (JEDEC)''' menu]]
When the process is complete the file the FPGA configuration file '''JEDEC''' is ready to use.
[[File:generate_data_file_jedec_from_diamond.png|center|thumb|700px| '''Generate Data File (JEDEC)''']]
= Programming the platform on FPG-EYE board = The last step is download the '''JEDEC''' file into ''FPG-EYE''. Please follow the [[Programming the FPG-EYE board]] istructions.

revision.text: As the first step download the Erika trunk where you will find the cal language libraries adapted to work on Erika Enterprise, system actors created in C language and a couple of demos that will be soon explained

As the first step download the Erika trunk where you will find the cal language libraries adapted to work on Erika Enterprise, system actors created in C language and a couple of demos that will be soon explained
Even if all the steps needed to run a demo application will be depicted, a preliminary knowledge on the actor's project and cal language will be useful to the reader.

As the first step download the Erika trunk where you will find the cal language libraries adapted to work on Erika Enterprise, system actors created in C language and a couple of demos that will be soon explained
Even if all the steps needed to run a demo application will be depicted, a preliminary knowledge on the actor's project and cal language will be useful to the reader.

This small tutorial describes the steps needed to launch a couple of demo applications with cal actors in Erika Enterprise using a Lattice Mico32 platform.
This tutorial has been tested on a board produced by Evidence in which we've integrated an FPGA using a Mico32 processor. The needed software has been installed and tested on Ubuntu 10.10 maverick but the installation process should be adapted to almost all other releases. For the purpose it has been used a virtual machine created with VMWare but all the test processes can be smoothly deployed on a physical linux machine.

Even if all the steps needed to run a demo application will be depicted, a preliminary knowledge on the actor's project and cal language will be useful to the reader. = Prerequisites = Make sure you have correctly installed both LatticeMico32 System and ispVM System on your Linux machine and exported all the environment variables needed for compiling a project. For any help please follow the following tutorial:
http://erika.tuxfamily.org/wiki/index.php?title=Tutorial:_Installing_CAL_with_ERIKA_Enterprise In order to compile a project it is essential to create a library for the Lattice Mico32 platform. We'll live the user the task to create its own library as he prefers. For our tests we've created an appropriate library called lib_camera_user that we placed inside the Erika's trunk in: ~/Evidence/Erika/ee/examples/mico32/demo/sw_projects. The needed software has been installed and tested on Ubuntu 10.10 maverick but the installation process should be adapted to almost all other releases. For the purpose it has been used a virtual machine created with VMWare but all the test processes can be smoothly deployed on a physical linux machine. Even if all the steps needed to run a demo application will be depicted, a preliminary knowledge on the actor's project and cal language will be useful to the reader. = Prerequisites = Make sure you have correctly installed both LatticeMico32 System and ispVM System on your Linux machine and exported all the environment variables needed for compiling a project. For any help please follow the following tutorial:
http://erika.tuxfamily.org/wiki/index.php?title=Tutorial:_Installing_CAL_with_ERIKA_Enterprise In order to compile a project it is essential to create a library for the Lattice Mico32 platform. We'll live the user the task to create its own library as he prefers. For our tests we've created an appropriate library called lib_camera_user that we placed inside the Erika's trunk in: ~/Evidence/Erika/ee/examples/mico32/demo/sw_projects. The user will have to use its own library and modify the conf.oil file into the project's directory to give the right relative path of the library itself. = Create your first project: cal_demo = We are now ready to create our first project and compile it. This first demo, called cal_demo, is composed of two system actors, a switch actor and a led actor called art_switch.c and art_led.c. These files are created in C language and can be found, along with the appropriate cal files, into Erika's tree in: ~/Evidence/Erika/ee/contrib/cal/src. The purpose of this demo is to read the state of the switches and the button present on the Erika's board and therefore produce this state switching on/off the appropriate leds on the board itself. Open the Lattice Mico32 System and press the C/C++ button on the status bar: [[File:eclipse_empty_screen.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows the C/C++ button that must be pressed]] Let's create a standard C project: [[File:eclipse-standard-make-project.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows the button which must be pressed to create a standard C project]] Give the project a name you like (i.e. cal_demo) and beware not to use the default location suggested by the program but the directory where resides the cal_demo into the Erika's trunk: [[File:cal-demo-project-settings.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows how to properly edit the project settings for the cal_demo project]] Press the Finish button and your project will be added to the list of C/C++ projects. To build the project right click on the cal_demo project and press the Build Project button: [[File:cal_demo_build_project.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows how to build the cal_demo project]] The result of the compilation is shown in the next picture: [[File:cal_demo_compilation_successful.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows the results of a correct building process]] At the end of the building process an output directory is created; here you can find the executable file out.elf To clean the project right click on the cal_demo project and press the Clean Project button: [[File:cal_demo_clean_project.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows how to clean a project]] = Create your second project: cal_demo_cal_actors = We are now ready to create our first project and compile it. This first demo, called cal_demo, is composed of two system actors, a switch actor and a led actor called art_switch.c and art_led.c. These files are created in C language and can be found, along with the appropriate cal files, into Erika's tree in: ~/Evidence/Erika/ee/contrib/cal/src. The purpose of this demo is to read the state of the switches and the button present on the Erika's board and therefore produce this state switching on/off the appropriate leds on the board itself.

http://erika.tuxfamily.org/wiki/index.php?title=Tutorial:_Installing_CAL_with_ERIKA_Enterprise In order to compile a project it is essential to create a library for the Lattice Mico32 platform. We'll leave the user the task to create its own library as he prefers. For our tests we've created an appropriate library called lib_camera_user that we placed inside the Erika's trunk in: ~/Evidence/Erika/ee/examples/mico32/demo/sw_projects. It will be up to the user to change appropriately the relative path of the library into the conf.oil that resides in the project's directory. = Create your first project: cal_demo = We are now ready to create our first project and compile it. This first demo, called cal_demo, is composed of two system actors, a switch actor and a led actor called art_switch.c and art_led.c. These files are created in C language and can be found, along with the appropriate cal files, into Erika's tree in: ~/Evidence/Erika/ee/contrib/cal/src. The two system actors are combined in a netlist file named switchled.nl that you can find into cal_demo's directory. The purpose of this demo is to read the state of the switches and button residing on the Erika's board and produce it switching on/off the appropriate leds on the board itself. Open the Lattice Mico32 System and press the C/C++ button on the status bar: [[File:eclipse_empty_screen.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows the C/C++ button that must be pressed]] Let's create a standard C project: [[File:eclipse-standard-make-project.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows the button which must be pressed to create a standard C project]] Give the project a name you like (i.e. cal_demo) and beware not to use the default location suggested by the program but the directory where resides the cal_demo into the Erika's trunk: [[File:cal-demo-project-settings.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows how to properly edit the project settings for the cal_demo project]] Press the Finish button and your project will be added to the list of C/C++ projects. To build the project right click on the cal_demo project and press the Build Project button: [[File:cal_demo_build_project.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows how to build the cal_demo project]] The result of the compilation is shown in the next picture: [[File:cal_demo_compilation_successful.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows the results of a correct building process]] At the end of the building process an output directory is created; here you can find the executable file out.elf To clean the project right click on the cal_demo project and press the Clean Project button: [[File:cal_demo_clean_project.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows how to clean a project]] = Create your second project: cal_demo_cal_actors = Let's create a second project composed of a cal actor named cal_demo_cal_actors. This demo is composed of both a system actor (the art_led.c already seen in the first demo) and a cal actor named gen.cal, a counter, that you can find into the cal_demo_cal_actor's directory. In the same directory you can find the genled.nl which is the netlist file that combines the two actors. The purpose of this demo is to visualize with the leds the number produced by the counter. In order to create the project follow the steps described in the previous example, just pay attention to the settings of the project: [[File:cal_demo_cal_actors_project_settings.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows how to properly edit the project settings for the cal_demo_cal_actors project]] Also the steps to build and clean the project are the same as the ones followed in the cal_demo project.

= Create your first project: cal_demo =
We are now ready to create our first project and compile it. This first demo, called cal_demo, is composed of two system actors, a switch actor and a led actor called <tt>art_switch.c</tt> and <tt>art_led.c</tt>. These files are created in C language and can be found, along with the appropriate CAL files, into Erika's repository in: <tt>~/Evidence/Erika/ee/contrib/cal/src</tt>. The two system actors are combined in a netlist file named <tt>switchled.nl</tt> that you can find into cal_demo's directory. The purpose of this demo is to read the state of the switches and button residing on the FPG-EYE and produce it switching on/off the appropriate leds on the board itself.
Open the Lattice Mico32 System and press the C/C++ button on the status bar: [[File:eclipse_empty_screen.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows the C/C++ button that must be pressed]]
Let's create a standard C project: [[File:eclipse-standard-make-project.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows the button which must be pressed to create a standard C project]]
Give the project a name you like (i.e. cal_demo) and beware not to use the default location suggested by the program but the directory where resides the cal_demo into the Erika's trunk: [[File:cal-demo-project-settings.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows how to properly edit the project settings for the cal_demo project]] Press the Finish button and your project will be added to the list of C/C++ projects.
Here's how your newly created project appears:
To build the project right click on the cal_demo project and press the Build Project button: [[File:cal_demo_build_project.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows how to build the cal_demo project]]
The result of the compilation is shown in the next screenshot: [[File:cal_demo_compilation_successful.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows the results of a correct building process]]
At the end of the building process an <tt>output</tt> directory is created; here you can find the executable file <tt>out.elf</tt>
To clean the project right click on the cal_demo project and press the Clean Project button: [[File:cal_demo_clean_project.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows how to clean a project]]

= Create your first project: cal_demo =
We are now ready to create our first project and compile it. This first demo, called cal_demo, is composed of two system actors, a switch actor and a led actor called <tt>art_switch.c</tt> and <tt>art_led.c</tt>. These files are created in C language and can be found, along with the appropriate CAL files, into Erika's repository in: <tt>~/Evidence/Erika/ee/contrib/cal/src</tt>. The two system actors are combined in a netlist file named <tt>switchled.nl</tt> that you can find into cal_demo's directory. The purpose of this demo is to read the state of the switches and button residing on the FPG-EYE and produce it switching on/off the appropriate leds on the board itself.
Open the Lattice Mico32 System and press the C/C++ button on the status bar: [[File:eclipse_empty_screen.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows the C/C++ button that must be pressed]]
Let's create a standard C project: [[File:eclipse-standard-make-project.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows the button which must be pressed to create a standard C project]]
Give the project a name you like (i.e. cal_demo) and beware not to use the default location suggested by the program but the directory where resides the cal_demo into the Erika's trunk: [[File:cal-demo-project-settings.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows how to properly edit the project settings for the cal_demo project]] Press the Finish button and your project will be added to the list of C/C++ projects.
Here's how your newly created project appears: [[File:cal_demo_project_created.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows the files you will find once created a new cal_demo project]] The files listed are: * main.c: main file project needed to initialize components of the FPG-EYE that will be used in the project. The user can place here it's own code. * switchled.nl: the netlist file listing the actors present in our CAL project * conf.oil: configuration file, part of the OSEK/VDX standard, that is used for OS and application configuration. You will find here, as application sources, both main.c and switchled.nl files. For a deeper explanation about OIL files have a look at [[Tutorial: RT-Druid and OIL basics | this tutorial]] * makefile: makefile of our project * crt0ram.S: file that implements boot-code and exception handlers
To build the project right click on the cal_demo project and press the Build Project button: [[File:cal_demo_build_project.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows how to build the cal_demo project]]
The result of the compilation is shown in the next screenshot: [[File:cal_demo_compilation_successful.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows the results of a correct building process]]
At the end of the building process an <tt>output</tt> directory is created; here you can find the executable file <tt>out.elf</tt>
To clean the project right click on the cal_demo project and press the Clean Project button: [[File:cal_demo_clean_project.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows how to clean a project]]

Open the Lattice Mico32 System and press the C/C++ button on the status bar: [[File:eclipse_empty_screen.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows the C/C++ button that must be pressed]]
Let's create a standard C project: [[File:eclipse-standard-make-project.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows the button which must be pressed to create a standard C project]]

[[File:cal_demo_cal_actors_project_settings.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows how to properly edit the project settings for the cal_demo_cal_actors project]]

Here's how your newly created project appears: [[File:cal_demo_project_created.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows the files you will find once created a new cal_demo project]] The files present at this stage of the project are: * main.c: main file project needed to initialize components of the FPG-EYE that will be used in the project. The user can place here it's own code. * switchled.nl: the netlist file listing the actors present in our CAL project. To better understand where the system actors were injected into ERIKA's repository and where newly created CAL actors have to be saved have a look [[CAL support on ERIKA Enterprise | here]] * conf.oil: configuration file, part of the OSEK/VDX standard, that is used for OS and application configuration. You will find here, as application sources, both main.c and switchled.nl files. * makefile: makefile of our project * crt0ram.S: file that implements boot-code and exception handlers

The result of the compilation is shown in the next screenshot: [[File:cal_demo_compilation_successful.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows the results of a correct building process]] As you can see in the previous screenshot there's a newly created folder named <tt>output</tt>. Here you can find: * obj: folder where object and dependency files are placed * switchled.depend and switchled.xdf: these files are automatically created by the ACTORS toolchain in the process of creating the switchled.c from the netlist file present in our project * out.elf: the executable file
To clean the project right click on the cal_demo project and press the Clean Project button: [[File:cal_demo_clean_project.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows how to clean a project]]
= Create your second project: cal_demo_cal_actors =
The main point of this second demo is that we used a CAL actor named <tt>gen.cal</tt>, a counter, instead of the previously used <tt>art_switch.c</tt> system actor; our counter is combined with the <tt>art_led.c</tt> system actor by the <tt>genled.nl</tt>. Both the netlist and the CAL actor files are placed in the project's directory. The purpose of this demo is to visualize the number produced by the counter switching on/off appropriately the leds placed into the FPG-EYE board
In order to create the project follow the steps described in the previous example, paying attention to the settings of the project:
[[File:cal_demo_cal_actors_project_settings.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows how to properly edit the project settings for the cal_demo_cal_actors project]]
Here's how your newly created project appears: [[File:cal_demo_cal_actors_project_created.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows the files you will find once created a new cal_demo_cal_actors project]]
Looking at the files present at this stage and comparing them with the previous cal_demo example the main differences you will note are: * gen.cal: this is the CAL actor * genled.nl: this is the new netlist file. Please note the different nomenclature it to be used to address a system actor or a CAL one. To fully understand the meaning of the this nomenclature please refer to [[CAL support on ERIKA Enterprise | this tutorial]] * conf.oil: the application sources now present are main.c and genled.nl.

This first demo, called cal_demo, is composed of two system actors, a switch actor and a led actor called <tt>art_switch.c</tt> and <tt>art_led.c</tt>. These files are created in C language and can be found, along with the appropriate CAL files, into Erika's repository in: <tt>~/Evidence/Erika/ee/contrib/cal/src</tt>. The two system actors are combined in a netlist file named <tt>switchled.nl</tt> that you can find into cal_demo's directory. The purpose of this demo is to read the state of the switches and button residing on the FPG-EYE and produce it switching on/off the appropriate leds on the board itself.
Open the Lattice Mico32 System and press the C/C++ button on the status bar: [[File:eclipse_empty_screen.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows the C/C++ button that must be pressed]]
Let's create a standard C project: [[File:eclipse-standard-make-project.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows the button which must be pressed to create a standard C project]]
Give the project a name you like (i.e. cal_demo) and beware not to use the default location suggested by the program but the directory where resides the cal_demo into the Erika's trunk: [[File:cal-demo-project-settings.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows how to properly edit the project settings for the cal_demo project]] Press the Finish button and your project will be added to the list of C/C++ projects.
Here's how your newly created project appears: [[File:cal_demo_project_created.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows the files you will find once created a new cal_demo project]] The files present at this stage of the project are: * main.c: main file project needed to initialize components of the FPG-EYE that will be used in the project. The user can place here it's own code. * switchled.nl: the netlist file listing the actors present in our CAL project; it's because of netlist files that actors will be automatically included in the building process. To better understand where the system actors were injected into ERIKA's repository and where newly created CAL actors have to be saved have a look [[CAL support on ERIKA Enterprise | here]] * conf.oil: configuration file, part of the OSEK/VDX standard, that is used for OS and application configuration. You will find here, as application sources, both main.c and switchled.nl files. * makefile: makefile of our project * crt0ram.S: file that implements boot-code and exception handlers
To build the project right click on the cal_demo project and press the Build Project button: [[File:cal_demo_build_project.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows how to build the cal_demo project]]
The result of the compilation is shown in the next screenshot: [[File:cal_demo_compilation_successful.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows the results of a correct building process]] As you can see in the previous screenshot there's a newly created folder named <tt>output/folder</tt> where object and dependency files are placed. Here you can find: * <tt>switchled.depend</tt> and <tt>switchled.xdf</tt>: these files are automatically created by the ACTORS makefiles in the process of creating the <tt>switchled.c</tt> from the netlist file present in our project * out.elf: the executable file
To clean the project right click on the cal_demo project and press the Clean Project button: [[File:cal_demo_clean_project.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows how to clean a project]]
= Create your second project: cal_demo_cal_actors =
The main point of this second demo is that we used a CAL actor named <tt>gen.cal</tt>, a counter, instead of the previously used <tt>art_switch.c</tt> system actor; our counter is combined with the <tt>art_led.c</tt> system actor by the <tt>genled.nl</tt>. Both the netlist and the CAL actor files are placed in the project's directory. The purpose of this demo is to visualize the number produced by the counter switching on/off appropriately the leds placed into the FPG-EYE board
In order to create the project follow the steps described in the previous example, paying attention to the settings of the project:
[[File:cal_demo_cal_actors_project_settings.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows how to properly edit the project settings for the cal_demo_cal_actors project]]
Here's how your newly created project appears: [[File:cal_demo_cal_actors_project_created.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows the files you will find once created a new cal_demo_cal_actors project]]
Looking at the files present at this stage and comparing them with the previous cal_demo example the main differences you will note are: * gen.cal: this is the CAL actor * genled.nl: this is the new netlist file. Please note the different nomenclature it to be used to address a system actor or a CAL one. To fully understand the meaning of the this nomenclature please refer to [[CAL support on ERIKA Enterprise | this tutorial]] * conf.oil: the application sources now present are main.c and genled.nl.
The result of a successful compilation (to be undertaken as explained in the previous example) is shown in the next screenshot: [[File:cal_demo_cal_actors_compilation_successful.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows the results of a correct building process of the cal_demo_cal_actors project]]
Looking at the newly created files you will notice some differences comparing with the previous example: * <tt>output/obj</tt>: there is now <tt>gen_0.c</tt> which is the C file created from the <tt>gen.cal</tt> CAL actor. In the process of obtaing <tt>gen_0.c</tt> and <tt>genled.c</tt> files the ACTORS makefiles created also <tt>gen_0.xlim</tt>, <tt>gen_0.par</tt> and <tt>art_led_0.par</tt> files that are stored into the project's directory.

[[File:cal_demo_cal_actors_project_settings.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows how to properly edit the project settings for the cal_demo_cal_actors project]]
