revision.text:
= Introduction = This tutorial describes the steps needed to integrate the CAL language into Erika Enterprise in order to create projects to be compiled and run in a Lattice Mico32 platform. The tutorial has been tested on a board produced by Evidence in which we've integrated an FPGA using a Mico32 processor. The needed software has been installed and tested on a virtual machine running Ubuntu 10.10 maverick but the installation process could be adapted to almost all other releases. The tests can moreover be smoothly deployed on a physical Linux machine. = Note for Linux Users = Since it has to be used a Linux distribution please look carefully at the following warnings: # The Evidence package installation path should NOT contain directory name with spaces. e.g. use ~/Evidence. # The actorsproject package installation path should NOT contain directory name with spaces: e.g. use ~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject. # It is strongly encouraged to adopt real paths instead of using symbolic links and aliases. # Please install all the actor's project compilers into their default directory, for instance ~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject/bin if the actor's project is located in ~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject = Prerequisites = In order to download the Erika's source code create an account in
http://http://erika.tuxfamily.org/ We will assume for our tutorial that you've created an account with username: erikauser Create then a virtual machine with Ubuntu 10.10 maverick as guest operating system. In our example we've used VMware Player 3.1.3 and installed WMware tools for linux version 8.4.5 version. Anyway all the tests can be smoothly deployed on a Linux physical machine. After creating the virtual machine, before proceeding with the installation process, it would be useful to completely update the packages installed in your system to the latest version. To update all the packages open a Terminal window and execute the following commands: 
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get upgrade
Now install all the packages needed to compile our projects. Type: 
sudo apt-get install java-common sun-java6-bin sun-java6-jre sun-java6-jdk sun-java6-source
sudo apt-get install ant subversion csh gawk libxml2-dev libsdl1.2-dev libgtk2.0-dev
= Downloading actor's project source code = You are now ready to download the actor's project on your system on a folder created for this purpose (i.e. ~/opendf): 
mkdir opendf
cd opendf
svn co https://opendf.svn.sourceforge.net/svnroot/opendf/trunk
Under the opendf's project trunk you will find all the actor's project source code needed for our purpose: ~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject. Move to this directory and install the tools provided by the actor's project by writing in a Terminal window: 
make
make install
Now you have all the tools needed to convert cal files into c files (xlim2c compiler and others) under the directory:~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject/bin = Installing ERIKA Enterprise and RT-Druid on Linux = In order to install ERIKA Enterprise and RT-Druid on Linux follow the procedure described here:
http://erika.tuxfamily.org/wiki/index.php?title=Tutorial:_Installing_ERIKA_and_RT-Druid_on_a_Linux_host For our tests we've used the eclipse_3_6_ready_to_use_LINUX_201101111314 version and installed it under the ~/Evidence folder so that you can find the eclipse directory under ~/Evidence/eclipse = Installing LatticeMico32 System and ispVM System on Linux = The LatticeMico32 System can be found at downloaded at the following website:
http://www.latticesemi.com/; for our tutorial we've chosen the 8.0.00.63 version for Linux. Download the related tar archive and put it on your hard disk, for instance in ~/temp_lattice. After having created in your home the ~/Lattice folder follow the steps reported below: 
cd ~/temp_lattice
tar xf RL8.0.00.63.43.09_linux_lm32.tar
cd ../Lattice/
../temp_lattice/RL8.0.00.63.43.09_lm32/mico32_install.csh /home/user/temp_lattice/RL8.0.00.63.43.09_lm32
rm -R ~/temp_lattice
Accept all the terms and agreements you will be prompted. When asked, tell the setup to install both gtool and Lattice Mico32 system Tools and point out you are not installing neither from a dvd drive, nor from a cd one. Next install ispVM System on your virtual machine. To do so download the ispVM System from the Lattice's website, for our tests we've used the 17.6 version for Linux. Put the ispvm_v17_6_linux.tar.gz file on a newly ~/temp_ispvm directory, create the ~/Lattice/ispvm folder and follow the steps reported below: 
cd ~/temp_ispvm
tar -xvzf ispvm_v17_6_linux.tar.gz 
mv isptools/ ../Lattice/ispvm/
cd ~ && rm -R ~/temp_ispvm

Create an appropriate folder, for instance ~/Evidence/Erika and type: 
cd ~/Evidence/Erika
svn co svn+ssh://erikauser@svn.tuxfamily.org/svnroot/erika/erikae/repos/ee/trunk/ee
= Export needed environment variables = Before launching for the first time the LatticeMico32 System we have to create and export some environment variables needed to compile projects into LatticeMico32 System. Open up the ~/.profile file with a text editor (i.e. Gedit) and append the following lines: 
export ISPVM_DIR=/home/user/Lattice/ispvm/isptools/ispvmsystem/
export RTDRUID_ECLIPSE_HOME=/home/user/Evidence/eclipse
export EEBASE=/home/user/Evidence/Erika/ee
export CAL_BASE=/home/user/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject
export ACTORS_JAVA=/usr/bin/java
Open a new Terminal window and export the newly created environment variables: 
export ISPVM_DIR=/home/user/Lattice/ispvm/isptools/ispvmsystem/
export RTDRUID_ECLIPSE_HOME=/home/user/Evidence/eclipse
export EEBASE=/home/user/Evidence/Erika/ee
export CAL_BASE=/home/user/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject
export ACTORS_JAVA=/usr/bin/java
Or, if you prefer, reboot your system. = Launch LatticeMico32 System = Employing the same Terminal window used previously to export the needed environment variables move to the directory where LatticeMico32 System resides and launch the executable file: 
cd ~/Lattice/micosystem
./LatticeMico32Launcher

The tests can moreover be smoothly deployed on a physical Linux machine. = Note for Linux Users = Since it has to be used a Linux distribution please look carefully at the following warnings: # The Evidence package installation path should NOT contain directory name with spaces. e.g. use ~/Evidence. # The actorsproject package installation path should NOT contain directory name with spaces: e.g. use ~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject. # It is strongly encouraged to adopt real paths instead of using symbolic links and aliases. # Please install all the actor's project compilers into their default directory, for instance ~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject/bin if the actor's project is located in ~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject = Prerequisites = In order to download the Erika's source code create an account in
http://http://erika.tuxfamily.org/ We will assume for our tutorial that you've created an account with username: erikauser Create then a virtual machine with Ubuntu 10.10 maverick as guest operating system. In our example we've used VMware Player 3.1.3 and installed WMware tools for linux version 8.4.5 version. Anyway all the tests can be smoothly deployed on a Linux physical machine. After creating the virtual machine, before proceeding with the installation process, it would be useful to completely update the packages installed in your system to the latest version. To update all the packages open a Terminal window and execute the following commands: 
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get upgrade
Now install all the packages needed to compile our projects. Type: 
sudo apt-get install java-common sun-java6-bin sun-java6-jre sun-java6-jdk sun-java6-source
sudo apt-get install ant subversion csh gawk libxml2-dev libsdl1.2-dev libgtk2.0-dev
= Downloading actor's project source code = You are now ready to download the actor's project on your system on a folder created for this purpose (i.e. ~/opendf): 
mkdir opendf
cd opendf
svn co https://opendf.svn.sourceforge.net/svnroot/opendf/trunk
Under the opendf's project trunk you will find all the actor's project source code needed for our purpose: ~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject. Move to this directory and install the tools provided by the actor's project by writing in a Terminal window: 
make
make install
Now you have all the tools needed to convert cal files into c files (xlim2c compiler and others) under the directory:~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject/bin = Installing ERIKA Enterprise and RT-Druid on Linux = In order to install ERIKA Enterprise and RT-Druid on Linux follow the procedure described here:
http://erika.tuxfamily.org/wiki/index.php?title=Tutorial:_Installing_ERIKA_and_RT-Druid_on_a_Linux_host For our tests we've used the eclipse_3_6_ready_to_use_LINUX_201101111314 version and installed it under the ~/Evidence folder so that you can find the eclipse directory under ~/Evidence/eclipse = Installing LatticeMico32 System and ispVM System on Linux = The LatticeMico32 System can be found at downloaded at the following website:
http://www.latticesemi.com/; for our tutorial we've chosen the 8.0.00.63 version for Linux. Download the related tar archive and put it on your hard disk, for instance in ~/temp_lattice. After having created in your home the ~/Lattice folder follow the steps reported below: 
cd ~/temp_lattice
tar xf RL8.0.00.63.43.09_linux_lm32.tar
cd ../Lattice/
../temp_lattice/RL8.0.00.63.43.09_lm32/mico32_install.csh /home/user/temp_lattice/RL8.0.00.63.43.09_lm32
rm -R ~/temp_lattice
Accept all the terms and agreements you will be prompted. When asked, tell the setup to install both gtool and Lattice Mico32 system Tools and point out you are not installing neither from a dvd drive, nor from a cd one. Next install ispVM System on your virtual machine. To do so download the ispVM System from the Lattice's website (for our tutorial we've used the 17.6 version for Linux). Put the ispvm_v17_6_linux.tar.gz file on a newly created ~/temp_ispvm directory, create the ~/Lattice/ispvm folder and follow the steps reported below: 
cd ~/temp_ispvm
tar -xvzf ispvm_v17_6_linux.tar.gz 
mv isptools/ ../Lattice/ispvm/
cd ~ && rm -R ~/temp_ispvm
= Downloading Erika's trunk = This step consists on downloading the Erika's trunk: here you will find the cal language libraries (specifically adapted to work in Erika Enterprise), system actors created in C language and a couple of demos that can be compiled and run. Create an appropriate folder, for instance ~/Evidence/Erika and type: 
cd ~/Evidence/Erika
svn co svn+ssh://erikauser@svn.tuxfamily.org/svnroot/erika/erikae/repos/ee/trunk/ee
= Export needed environment variables = Before launching for the first time the LatticeMico32 System we have to create and export some environment variables needed to compile projects into LatticeMico32 System. Open up the ~/.profile file with a text editor (i.e. Gedit) and append the following lines: 
export ISPVM_DIR=/home/user/Lattice/ispvm/isptools/ispvmsystem/
export RTDRUID_ECLIPSE_HOME=/home/user/Evidence/eclipse
export EEBASE=/home/user/Evidence/Erika/ee
export CAL_BASE=/home/user/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject
export ACTORS_JAVA=/usr/bin/java
Open a new Terminal window and export the newly created environment variables: 
export ISPVM_DIR=/home/user/Lattice/ispvm/isptools/ispvmsystem/
export RTDRUID_ECLIPSE_HOME=/home/user/Evidence/eclipse
export EEBASE=/home/user/Evidence/Erika/ee
export CAL_BASE=/home/user/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject
export ACTORS_JAVA=/usr/bin/java
Or, if you prefer, reboot your system. = Launch LatticeMico32 System = Employing the same Terminal window used previously to export the needed environment variables move to the directory where LatticeMico32 System resides and launch the executable file: 
cd ~/Lattice/micosystem
./LatticeMico32Launcher

Next install ispVM System on your virtual machine. To do so download the ispVM System from the Lattice's website (for our tutorial we've used the 17.6 version for Linux). Put the ispvm_v17_6_linux.tar.gz file on a newly created ~/temp_ispvm directory, create the ~/Lattice/ispvm folder and follow the steps reported below: 
cd ~/temp_ispvm
tar -xvzf ispvm_v17_6_linux.tar.gz 
mv isptools/ ../Lattice/ispvm/
cd ~ && rm -R ~/temp_ispvm
= Downloading Erika's trunk = This step consists on downloading the Erika's trunk: here you will find, among a lot of things, the cal language libraries (specifically adapted to work in Erika Enterprise), system actors created in C language and a couple of demos that can be compiled and run. Create an appropriate folder, for instance ~/Evidence/Erika and type: 
cd ~/Evidence/Erika
svn co svn+ssh://erikauser@svn.tuxfamily.org/svnroot/erika/erikae/repos/ee/trunk/ee
= Exporting environment variables = Before launching for the first time the LatticeMico32 System we have to create and export some environment variables needed to compile projects into LatticeMico32 System. Open the ~/.profile file with a text editor (i.e. Gedit) and append the following lines: 
export ISPVM_DIR=/home/user/Lattice/ispvm/isptools/ispvmsystem/
export RTDRUID_ECLIPSE_HOME=/home/user/Evidence/eclipse
export EEBASE=/home/user/Evidence/Erika/ee
export CAL_BASE=/home/user/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject
export ACTORS_JAVA=/usr/bin/java
Open a new Terminal window and export the newly created environment variables by copying the very same lines you've just added. Or, if you prefer, reboot your system. = Launch LatticeMico32 System = Employing the same Terminal window used previously to export the needed environment variables move to the directory where LatticeMico32 System resides and launch the executable file: 
cd ~/Lattice/micosystem
./LatticeMico32Launcher

= Introduction = This tutorial describes the steps needed to integrate the CAL language into Erika Enterprise in order to create projects to be compiled and run in a Lattice Mico32 platform. The tutorial has been tested on a board produced by Evidence in which we've integrated an FPGA using a Mico32 processor. The needed software has been installed and tested on a virtual machine running Ubuntu 10.10 maverick but the installation process could be adapted to almost all other releases. The tests can moreover be smoothly deployed on a physical Linux machine. = Note for Linux Users = Since it has to be used a Linux distribution please look carefully at the following warnings: # The Evidence package installation path should NOT contain directory name with spaces. e.g. use ~/Evidence. # The actorsproject package installation path should NOT contain directory name with spaces: e.g. use ~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject. # It is strongly encouraged to adopt real paths instead of using symbolic links and aliases. # Please install all the actor's project compilers into their default directory, for instance ~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject/bin if the actor's project is located in ~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject = Prerequisites = In order to download the Erika's source code create an account in
http://http://erika.tuxfamily.org/ We will assume for our tutorial that you've created an account with username: erikauser Create then a virtual machine with Ubuntu 10.10 maverick as guest operating system. In our example we've used VMware Player 3.1.3 and installed WMware tools for linux version 8.4.5 version. Anyway all the tests can be smoothly deployed on a Linux physical machine. After creating the virtual machine, before proceeding with the installation process, it would be useful to completely update the packages installed in your system to the latest version. To update all the packages open a Terminal window and execute the following commands: 
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get upgrade
Now install all the packages needed to compile our projects. Type: 
sudo apt-get install java-common sun-java6-bin sun-java6-jre sun-java6-jdk sun-java6-source
sudo apt-get install ant subversion csh gawk libxml2-dev libsdl1.2-dev libgtk2.0-dev
= Downloading actor's project source code = You are now ready to download the actor's project on your system on a folder created for this purpose (i.e. ~/opendf): 
mkdir opendf
cd opendf
svn co https://opendf.svn.sourceforge.net/svnroot/opendf/trunk
Under the opendf's project trunk you will find all the actor's project source code needed for our purpose: ~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject. Move to this directory and install the tools provided by the actor's project by writing in a Terminal window: 
make
make install

http://www.latticesemi.com/; for our tutorial we've chosen the 8.0.00.63 version for Linux. Download the related tar archive and put it on your hard disk, for instance in ~/temp_lattice. After having created in your home the ~/Lattice folder follow the steps reported below:

../temp_lattice/RL8.0.00.63.43.09_lm32/mico32_install.csh /home/user/temp_lattice/RL8.0.00.63.43.09_lm32
rm -R ~/temp_lattice
Accept all the terms and agreements you will be prompted. http://www.latticesemi.com/; for our tutorial we've chosen the 8.0.00.63 version for Linux. Download the related tar archive and put it on your hard disk, for instance in ~/temp_lattice. After having created in your home the ~/Lattice folder follow the steps reported below: 
cd ~/temp_lattice
tar xf RL8.0.00.63.43.09_linux_lm32.tar
cd ../Lattice/
../temp_lattice/RL8.0.00.63.43.09_lm32/mico32_install.csh /home/user/temp_lattice/RL8.0.00.63.43.09_lm32
rm -R ~/temp_lattice
Accept all the terms and agreements you will be prompted. When asked, tell the setup to install both gtool and Lattice Mico32 system Tools and point out you are not installing neither from a dvd drive, nor from a cd one. Next install ispVM System on your virtual machine. To do so download the ispVM System from the Lattice's website (for our tutorial we've used the 17.6 version for Linux). Put the ispvm_v17_6_linux.tar.gz file on a newly created ~/temp_ispvm directory, create the ~/Lattice/ispvm folder and follow the steps reported below: 
cd ~/temp_ispvm
tar -xvzf ispvm_v17_6_linux.tar.gz 
mv isptools/ ../Lattice/ispvm/
cd ~ && rm -R ~/temp_ispvm
= Downloading Erika's trunk = This step consists on downloading the Erika's trunk: here you will find, among a lot of things, the cal language libraries (specifically adapted to work in Erika Enterprise), system actors created in C language and a couple of demos that can be compiled and run. Create an appropriate folder, for instance ~/Evidence/Erika and type: 
cd ~/Evidence/Erika
svn co svn+ssh://erikauser@svn.tuxfamily.org/svnroot/erika/erikae/repos/ee/trunk/ee
= Exporting environment variables = Before launching for the first time the LatticeMico32 System we have to create and export some environment variables needed to compile projects into LatticeMico32 System. Open the ~/.profile file with a text editor (i.e. Gedit) and append the following lines: 
export ISPVM_DIR=/home/user/Lattice/ispvm/isptools/ispvmsystem/
export RTDRUID_ECLIPSE_HOME=/home/user/Evidence/eclipse
export EEBASE=/home/user/Evidence/Erika/ee
export CAL_BASE=/home/user/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject
export ACTORS_JAVA=/usr/bin/java
Open a new Terminal window and export the newly created environment variables by copying the very same lines you've just added. Or, if you prefer, reboot your system. = Launch LatticeMico32 System = Employing the same Terminal window used previously to export the environment variables move to the directory where LatticeMico32 System resides and launch the executable file: 
cd ~/Lattice/micosystem
./LatticeMico32Launcher

For more information about CAL language and actors visit the ACTORS [http://www.actors-project.eu/ website] OpenDF, whose site is visible [http://sourceforge.net/projects/opendf/ here], is an environment for building and executing actor/dataflow models, including support for the CAL actor language. The tutorial has been tested on the FPG-EYE board produced by Evidence in which we've integrated an FPGA using a Mico32 processor. The operating system chosen is an Ubuntu 10.10 maverick running on a virtual machine, anyway the installation process could be adapted to almost all other Linux releases on virtual or physical machines. = Note for Linux Users = Since it has to be used a Linux distribution please look carefully at the following warnings: # The Evidence package installation path should NOT contain directory name with spaces. e.g. use ~/Evidence. # The actorsproject package installation path should NOT contain directory name with spaces: e.g. use ~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject. # It is strongly encouraged to adopt real paths instead of using symbolic links and aliases. # Please install all the actor's project compilers into their default directory, for instance ~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject/bin if the actor's project is located in ~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject = Prerequisites = In order to download the Erika's source code you can create an account in
http://http://erika.tuxfamily.org/ If preferred, make a SVN anonymous access as described in
http://erika.tuxfamily.org/wiki/index.php?title=ERIKA_Enterprise_and_RT-Druid_SVN_Access In the following we will assume you've created an account with username: erikauser Create then a virtual machine with Ubuntu 10.10 maverick as guest operating system. In our example we've used VMware Player 3.1.3 and installed WMware tools for linux version 8.4.5 version. Anyway all the tests can be smoothly deployed on a Linux physical machine. After creating the virtual machine, before proceeding with the installation process, it would be useful to completely update the packages installed in your system to the latest version. To update all the packages open a Terminal window and execute the following commands: 
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get upgrade
Now install all the packages needed to compile our projects. Type: 
sudo apt-get install java-common sun-java6-bin sun-java6-jre sun-java6-jdk sun-java6-source
sudo apt-get install ant subversion csh gawk libxml2-dev libsdl1.2-dev libgtk2.0-dev
= Downloading actor's project source code = You are now ready to download the actor's project on your system on a folder created for this purpose (i.e. ~/opendf): 
mkdir opendf
cd opendf
svn co https://opendf.svn.sourceforge.net/svnroot/opendf/trunk
Under the opendf's project trunk you will find all the actor's project source code needed for our purpose: ~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject. Move to this directory and install the tools provided by the actor's project by writing in a Terminal window: 
make
make install
Now you have all the tools needed to convert cal files into c files (xlim2c compiler and others) under the directory:~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject/bin = Installing ERIKA Enterprise and RT-Druid on Linux = In order to install ERIKA Enterprise and RT-Druid on Linux follow the procedure described here:
http://erika.tuxfamily.org/wiki/index.php?title=Tutorial:_Installing_ERIKA_and_RT-Druid_on_a_Linux_host For our tests we've used the eclipse_3_6_ready_to_use_LINUX_201101111314 version and installed it under the ~/Evidence folder so that you can find the eclipse directory under ~/Evidence/eclipse = Installing LatticeMico32 System and ispVM System on Linux = The LatticeMico32 System can be found at downloaded at the following website:
http://www.latticesemi.com/; for our tutorial we've chosen the 8.0.00.63 version for Linux. Download the related tar archive and put it on your hard disk, for instance in ~/temp_lattice. After having created in your home the ~/Lattice folder follow the steps reported below: 
cd ~/temp_lattice
tar xf RL8.0.00.63.43.09_linux_lm32.tar
cd ../Lattice/
../temp_lattice/RL8.0.00.63.43.09_lm32/mico32_install.csh /home/user/temp_lattice/RL8.0.00.63.43.09_lm32
rm -R ~/temp_lattice
Accept all the terms and agreements you will be prompted. When asked, tell the setup to install both gtool and Lattice Mico32 system Tools and point out you are not installing neither from a dvd drive, nor from a cd one. Next install ispVM System on your virtual machine. To do so download the ispVM System from the Lattice's website (for our tutorial we've used the 17.6 version for Linux). Put the ispvm_v17_6_linux.tar.gz file on a newly created ~/temp_ispvm directory, create the ~/Lattice/ispvm folder and follow the steps reported below: 
cd ~/temp_ispvm
tar -xvzf ispvm_v17_6_linux.tar.gz 
mv isptools/ ../Lattice/ispvm/
cd ~ && rm -R ~/temp_ispvm
= Downloading Erika's trunk = This step consists on downloading the Erika's trunk: here you will find, among a lot of things, the cal language libraries (specifically adapted to work in Erika Enterprise), system actors created in C language and a couple of demos that can be compiled and run. Create an appropriate folder, for instance ~/Evidence/Erika and type: 
cd ~/Evidence/Erika
svn co svn+ssh://erikauser@svn.tuxfamily.org/svnroot/erika/erikae/repos/ee/trunk/ee
= Exporting environment variables = Before launching for the first time the LatticeMico32 System we have to create and export some environment variables needed to compile projects into LatticeMico32 System. Open the ~/.profile file with a text editor (i.e. Gedit) and append the following lines: 
export ISPVM_DIR=/home/user/Lattice/ispvm/isptools/ispvmsystem/
export RTDRUID_ECLIPSE_HOME=/home/user/Evidence/eclipse
export EEBASE=/home/user/Evidence/Erika/ee
export CAL_BASE=/home/user/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject
export ACTORS_JAVA=/usr/bin/java
Open a new Terminal window and export the newly created environment variables by copying the very same lines you've just added. Or, if you prefer, relog into your system. = Launch LatticeMico32 System = Employing the same Terminal window used previously to export the environment variables move to the directory where LatticeMico32 System resides and launch the executable file: 
cd ~/Lattice/micosystem
./LatticeMico32Launcher

tar xf RL8.0.00.63.43.09_linux_lm32.tar
cd ../Lattice/
../temp_lattice/RL8.0.00.63.43.09_lm32/mico32_install.csh /home/user/temp_lattice/RL8.0.00.63.43.09_lm32
rm -R ~/temp_lattice
Accept all the terms and agreements you will be prompted. When asked, tell the setup to install both gtool and Lattice Mico32 system Tools and point out you are not installing neither from a dvd drive, nor from a cd one. Next install ispVM System on your virtual machine. To do so download the ispVM System from the Lattice's website (for our tutorial we've used the 17.6 version for Linux). Put the ispvm_v17_6_linux.tar.gz file on a newly created ~/temp_ispvm directory, create the ~/Lattice/ispvm folder and follow the steps reported below: 
cd ~/temp_ispvm
tar -xvzf ispvm_v17_6_linux.tar.gz 
mv isptools/ ../Lattice/ispvm/
cd ~ && rm -R ~/temp_ispvm
= Downloading Erika's trunk = This step consists on downloading the Erika Enterprise repository: here you will find, among other things, the CAL language libraries (specifically adapted to work in Erika Enterprise), system actors created in C language and a couple of demos that can be compiled and run. To download the Erika's repository have a look at [[Tutorial: Installing ERIKA and RT-Druid on a Linux host]]. In the following steps we will assume you've correctly stored the Erika's repository in ~/Evidence/Erika = Exporting environment variables = Before launching for the first time the LatticeMico32 System we have to create and export some environment variables needed to compile projects into LatticeMico32 System. Open the ~/.profile file with a text editor (i.e. Gedit) and append the following lines: 
export ISPVM_DIR=/home/user/Lattice/ispvm/isptools/ispvmsystem/
export RTDRUID_ECLIPSE_HOME=/home/user/Evidence/eclipse
export EEBASE=/home/user/Evidence/Erika/ee
export CAL_BASE=/home/user/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject
export ACTORS_JAVA=/usr/bin/java
Open a new Terminal window and export the newly created environment variables by copying the very same lines you've just added. Or, if you prefer, relog into your system. = Launch LatticeMico32 System = Employing the same Terminal window used previously to export the environment variables move to the directory where LatticeMico32 System resides and launch the executable file: 
cd ~/Lattice/micosystem
./LatticeMico32Launcher

= Introduction = This tutorial describes all the steps to follow in order to install the tools needed to compile and run projects in CAL language on a Lattice Mico32 platform. For a brief introduction on the CAL language visit the following link: [[Brief introduction to the CAL language]] The tutorial has been tested on the FPG-EYE board produced by Evidence in which we've integrated an FPGA using a Mico32 processor. The operating system chosen is an Ubuntu 10.10 maverick running on a virtual machine, anyway the installation process could be adapted to almost all other Linux releases on virtual or physical machines. = Note for Linux Users = Since it has to be used a Linux distribution please look carefully at the following warnings: # The Evidence package installation path should NOT contain directory name with spaces. e.g. use ~/Evidence. # The actorsproject package installation path should NOT contain directory name with spaces: e.g. use ~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject. # It is strongly encouraged to adopt real paths instead of using symbolic links and aliases. # Please install all the actor's project compilers into their default directory, for instance ~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject/bin if the actor's project is located in ~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject = Prerequisites = In order to download the Erika's source code you can create an account in http://erika.tuxfamily.org/ If preferred, make a SVN anonymous access as described in
http://erika.tuxfamily.org/wiki/index.php?title=ERIKA_Enterprise_and_RT-Druid_SVN_Access In the following we will assume you've created an account with username: erikauser Create then a virtual machine with Ubuntu 10.10 maverick as guest operating system. In our example we've used VMware Player 3.1.3 and installed WMware tools for linux version 8.4.5 version. Anyway all the tests can be smoothly deployed on a Linux physical machine. After creating the virtual machine, before proceeding with the installation process, it would be useful to completely update the packages installed in your system to the latest version. To update all the packages open a Terminal window and execute the following commands: 
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get upgrade
Now install all the packages needed to compile our projects. Type: 
sudo apt-get install java-common sun-java6-bin sun-java6-jre sun-java6-jdk sun-java6-source
sudo apt-get install ant subversion csh gawk libxml2-dev libsdl1.2-dev libgtk2.0-dev
= Downloading actor's project source code = You are now ready to download the actor's project on your system on a folder created for this purpose (i.e. ~/opendf): 
mkdir opendf
cd opendf
svn co https://opendf.svn.sourceforge.net/svnroot/opendf/trunk
Under the opendf's project trunk you will find all the actor's project source code needed for our purpose: ~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject. Move to this directory and install the tools provided by the actor's project by writing in a Terminal window: 
make
make install

After creating the virtual machine, before proceeding with the installation process, it would be useful to completely update the packages installed in your system to the latest version. To update all the packages open a Terminal window and execute the following commands: 
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get upgrade
Now install all the packages needed to compile our projects. Type: 
sudo apt-get install java-common sun-java6-bin sun-java6-jre sun-java6-jdk sun-java6-source
sudo apt-get install ant subversion csh gawk libxml2-dev libsdl1.2-dev libgtk2.0-dev
= Downloading ACTORS project source code = You are now ready to download the actor's project on your system on a folder created for this purpose (i.e. ~/opendf): 
mkdir opendf
cd opendf
svn co https://opendf.svn.sourceforge.net/svnroot/opendf/trunk
Under the opendf's project trunk you will find all the actor's project source code needed for our purpose: ~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject. Move to this directory and install the tools provided by the actor's project by writing in a Terminal window: 
make
make install
Now you have all the tools needed to convert cal files into c files (xlim2c compiler and others) under the directory:~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject/bin = Installing ERIKA Enterprise and RT-Druid on Linux = In order to install ERIKA Enterprise and RT-Druid on Linux follow the procedure described here:
http://erika.tuxfamily.org/wiki/index.php?title=Tutorial:_Installing_ERIKA_and_RT-Druid_on_a_Linux_host For our tests we've used the eclipse_3_6_ready_to_use_LINUX_201101111314 version and installed it under the ~/Evidence folder so that you can find the eclipse directory under ~/Evidence/eclipse = Installing LatticeMico32 System and ispVM System on Linux = The LatticeMico32 System can be found at downloaded at the following website:
http://www.latticesemi.com/; for our tutorial we've chosen the 8.0.00.63 version for Linux. Download the related tar archive and put it on your hard disk, for instance in ~/temp_lattice. After having created in your home the ~/Lattice folder follow the steps reported below: 
cd ~/temp_lattice
tar xf RL8.0.00.63.43.09_linux_lm32.tar
cd ../Lattice/
../temp_lattice/RL8.0.00.63.43.09_lm32/mico32_install.csh /home/user/temp_lattice/RL8.0.00.63.43.09_lm32
rm -R ~/temp_lattice
Accept all the terms and agreements you will be prompted. When asked, tell the setup to install both gtool and Lattice Mico32 system Tools and point out you are not installing neither from a dvd drive, nor from a cd one. Next install ispVM System on your virtual machine. To do so download the ispVM System from the Lattice's website (for our tutorial we've used the 17.6 version for Linux). Put the ispvm_v17_6_linux.tar.gz file on a newly created ~/temp_ispvm directory, create the ~/Lattice/ispvm folder and follow the steps reported below: 
cd ~/temp_ispvm
tar -xvzf ispvm_v17_6_linux.tar.gz 
mv isptools/ ../Lattice/ispvm/
cd ~ && rm -R ~/temp_ispvm
= Downloading Erika's trunk = This step consists on downloading the Erika Enterprise repository: here you will find, among other things, the CAL language libraries (specifically adapted to work in Erika Enterprise), system actors created in C language and a couple of demos that can be compiled and run. To download the Erika's repository have a look at [[Tutorial: Installing ERIKA and RT-Druid on a Linux host | this tutorial]]. In the following steps we will assume you've correctly stored the Erika's repository in ~/Evidence/Erika = Exporting environment variables = Before launching for the first time the LatticeMico32 System we have to create and export some environment variables needed to compile projects into LatticeMico32 System. Open the ~/.profile file with a text editor (i.e. Gedit) and append the following lines: 
export ISPVM_DIR=/home/user/Lattice/ispvm/isptools/ispvmsystem/
export RTDRUID_ECLIPSE_HOME=/home/user/Evidence/eclipse
export EEBASE=/home/user/Evidence/Erika/ee
export CAL_BASE=/home/user/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject
export ACTORS_JAVA=/usr/bin/java
Open a new Terminal window and export the newly created environment variables by copying the very same lines you've just added. Or, if you prefer, relog into your system. = Launch LatticeMico32 System = Employing the same Terminal window used previously to export the environment variables move to the directory where LatticeMico32 System resides and launch the executable file: 
cd ~/Lattice/micosystem
./LatticeMico32Launcher

= Introduction = This tutorial describes all the steps to follow in order to install the tools needed to compile and run projects in CAL language on a Lattice Mico32 platform. For a brief introduction on the CAL language visit the [[Brief introduction to the CAL language | following link]] The tutorial has been tested on the FPG-EYE board produced by Evidence in which we've integrated an FPGA using a Mico32 processor. The operating system chosen is an Ubuntu 10.10 maverick running on a virtual machine, anyway the installation process could be adapted to almost all other Linux releases on virtual or physical machines. = Note for Linux Users = Since it has to be used a Linux distribution please look carefully at the following warnings: # The Evidence package installation path should NOT contain directory name with spaces. e.g. use ~/Evidence. # The actorsproject package installation path should NOT contain directory name with spaces: e.g. use ~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject. # It is strongly encouraged to adopt real paths instead of using symbolic links and aliases. # Please install all the ACTORS project compilers into their default directory. For instance, given the ACTORS project repository is installed in ~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject the compilers will have to be located in ~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject/bin = Prerequisites = As a first step you have to download the ERIKA's Enterprise repository where you will find, among other things, the CAL language libraries (specifically adapted to work in Erika Enterprise), system actors created in C language and a couple of demos that can be compiled and run. Secondly install ERIKA Enterprise and RT-Druid on Linux. Both steps can be accomplished just following [[Tutorial: Installing ERIKA and RT-Druid on a Linux host | this tutorial]]. In the follow-up of this tutorial we will assume that you've correctly stored the ERIKA's repository in ~/Evidence/Erika and installed the eclipse_3_6_ready_to_use_LINUX_201101111314 version of ERIKA'S Enterprise under the ~/Evidence folder, in order to find the eclipse directory under ~/Evidence/eclipse Create then a virtual machine with Ubuntu 10.10 maverick as guest operating system. In our example we've used VMware Player 3.1.3 and installed WMware tools for linux version 8.4.5 version. Anyway all the tests can be smoothly deployed on a Linux physical machine. After creating the virtual machine, before proceeding with the installation process, it would be useful to completely update the packages installed in your system to the latest version. To update all the packages open a Terminal window and execute the following commands: 
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get upgrade
Now install all the packages needed to compile our projects. Type: 
sudo apt-get install java-common sun-java6-bin sun-java6-jre sun-java6-jdk sun-java6-source
sudo apt-get install ant subversion csh gawk libxml2-dev libsdl1.2-dev libgtk2.0-dev
= Downloading ACTORS project source code = You are now ready to download the actor's project on your system on a folder created for this purpose (i.e. ~/opendf): 
mkdir opendf
cd opendf
svn co https://opendf.svn.sourceforge.net/svnroot/opendf/trunk
Under the opendf's project trunk you will find all the actor's project source code needed for our purpose: ~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject. Move to this directory and install the tools provided by the actor's project by writing in a Terminal window: 
make
make install
Now you have all the tools needed to convert cal files into c files (xlim2c compiler and others) under the directory:~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject/bin = Installing LatticeMico32 System and ispVM System on Linux = The LatticeMico32 System can be found at downloaded at the following website:
http://www.latticesemi.com/; for our tutorial we've chosen the 8.0.00.63 version for Linux. Download the related tar archive and put it on your hard disk, for instance in ~/temp_lattice. After having created in your home the ~/Lattice folder follow the steps reported below: 
cd ~/temp_lattice
tar xf RL8.0.00.63.43.09_linux_lm32.tar
cd ../Lattice/
../temp_lattice/RL8.0.00.63.43.09_lm32/mico32_install.csh /home/user/temp_lattice/RL8.0.00.63.43.09_lm32
rm -R ~/temp_lattice
Accept all the terms and agreements you will be prompted. When asked, tell the setup to install both gtool and Lattice Mico32 system Tools and point out you are not installing neither from a dvd drive, nor from a cd one. Next install ispVM System on your virtual machine. To do so download the ispVM System from the Lattice's website (for our tutorial we've used the 17.6 version for Linux). Put the ispvm_v17_6_linux.tar.gz file on a newly created ~/temp_ispvm directory, create the ~/Lattice/ispvm folder and follow the steps reported below: 
cd ~/temp_ispvm
tar -xvzf ispvm_v17_6_linux.tar.gz 
mv isptools/ ../Lattice/ispvm/
cd ~ && rm -R ~/temp_ispvm
= Exporting environment variables = Before launching for the first time the LatticeMico32 System we have to create and export some environment variables needed to compile projects into LatticeMico32 System. Open the ~/.profile file with a text editor (i.e. Gedit) and append the following lines: 
export ISPVM_DIR=/home/user/Lattice/ispvm/isptools/ispvmsystem/
export RTDRUID_ECLIPSE_HOME=/home/user/Evidence/eclipse
export EEBASE=/home/user/Evidence/Erika/ee
export CAL_BASE=/home/user/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject
export ACTORS_JAVA=/usr/bin/java
Open a new Terminal window and export the newly created environment variables by copying the very same lines you've just added. Or, if you prefer, relog into your system. = Launch LatticeMico32 System and compile a CAL application with ERIKA Enterprise = Employing the same Terminal window used previously to export the environment variables move to the directory where LatticeMico32 System resides and launch the executable file: 
cd ~/Lattice/micosystem
./LatticeMico32Launcher
Finally compile and run a CAL application with ERIKA Enterprise following [[Tutorial: Compiling a CAL application with ERIKA Enterprise | this tutorial]]

Or, if you prefer, relog into your system. = Launch LatticeMico32 System and compile a CAL application with ERIKA Enterprise = Employing the same Terminal window used previously to export the environment variables move to the directory where LatticeMico32 System resides and launch the executable file: 
cd ~/Lattice/micosystem

Finally compile and run a CAL application with ERIKA Enterprise following [[Tutorial: Compiling a CAL application with ERIKA Enterprise | this tutorial]]

= Introduction = This tutorial describes all the steps to follow in order to install the tools needed to compile and run projects in CAL language on a [http://www.latticesemi.com/products/intellectualproperty/ipcores/mico32/index.cfm Lattice Mico32 platform]. For a brief introduction on the CAL language visit the [[Brief introduction to the CAL language | following link]] The tutorial has been tested on the FPG-EYE board produced by Evidence in which we've integrated an FPGA using a Mico32 processor. The operating system chosen is an Ubuntu 10.10 maverick running on a virtual machine, anyway the installation process could be adapted to almost all other Linux releases on virtual or physical machines. = Note for Linux Users = Since it has to be used a Linux distribution please look carefully at the following warnings: # The Evidence package installation path should NOT contain directory name with spaces. e.g. use ~/Evidence. # The actorsproject package installation path should NOT contain directory name with spaces: e.g. use ~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject. # It is strongly encouraged to adopt real paths instead of using symbolic links and aliases. # Please install all the ACTORS project compilers into their default directory. For instance, given the ACTORS project repository is installed in ~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject the compilers will have to be located in ~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject/bin = Prerequisites = As a first step you have to download the ERIKA's Enterprise repository where you will find, among other things, the CAL language libraries (specifically adapted to work in Erika Enterprise), system actors created in C language and a couple of demos that can be compiled and run. Secondly install ERIKA Enterprise and RT-Druid on Linux. Both steps can be accomplished just following [[Tutorial: Installing ERIKA and RT-Druid on a Linux host | this tutorial]]. In the follow-up of this tutorial we will assume that you've correctly stored the ERIKA's repository in ~/Evidence/Erika and installed the eclipse_3_6_ready_to_use_LINUX_201101111314 version of ERIKA'S Enterprise under the ~/Evidence folder, in order to find the eclipse directory under ~/Evidence/eclipse Create then a virtual machine with Ubuntu 10.10 maverick as guest operating system. In our example we've used VMware Player 3.1.3 and installed WMware tools for linux version 8.4.5 version. Anyway all the tests can be smoothly deployed on a Linux physical machine. After creating the virtual machine, before proceeding with the installation process, it would be useful to completely update the packages installed in your system to the latest version. To update all the packages open a Terminal window and execute the following commands: 
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get upgrade
Now install all the packages that will be needed to compile our projects. Type: 
sudo apt-get install java-common sun-java6-bin sun-java6-jre sun-java6-jdk sun-java6-source
sudo apt-get install ant subversion csh gawk libxml2-dev libsdl1.2-dev libgtk2.0-dev
= Downloading the OpenDF repository and the ACTORS project source code = You are now ready to download the OpenDF repository on your system (i.e. in ~/opendf): 
mkdir opendf
cd opendf
svn co https://opendf.svn.sourceforge.net/svnroot/opendf/trunk
Under the OpenDF's project repository you will find all the ACTORS project source code needed for our purpose in: ~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject. Move to this directory and install the tools provided for the compilation of CAL projects by writing in a Terminal window: 
make
make install
Now you have all the tools needed to convert CAL files into C language (xlim2c compiler and others) under the directory:~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject/bin = Installing LatticeMico32 System and ispVM System on Linux = The LatticeMico32 System is used to implement the LatticeMico32 soft microprocessor and attached peripheral components in a Lattice FPGA. It contains integrated tools that combine with ispLEVER software (which includes ispVM System) to coordinate the building of an embedded processor system on an FPGA device and write the software to drive it. All the software we will use can be downloaded at [http://www.latticesemi.com this link]; for our tutorial we've chosen the 8.0.00.63 version for Linux. Download the related tar archive and put it on your hard disk, for instance in ~/temp_lattice. After having created in your home the ~/Lattice folder follow the steps reported below: 
cd ~/temp_lattice
tar xf RL8.0.00.63.43.09_linux_lm32.tar
cd ../Lattice/
../temp_lattice/RL8.0.00.63.43.09_lm32/mico32_install.csh /home/user/temp_lattice/RL8.0.00.63.43.09_lm32
rm -R ~/temp_lattice
Accept all the terms and agreements you will be prompted. When asked, tell the setup to install both gtool and Lattice Mico32 system Tools and point out you are not installing neither from a dvd drive, nor from a cd one. Next install ispVM System on your virtual machine. To do so download the ispVM System from the Lattice's website (for our tutorial we've used the 17.6 version for Linux). Put the ispvm_v17_6_linux.tar.gz file on a newly created ~/temp_ispvm directory, create the ~/Lattice/ispvm folder and follow the steps reported below: 
cd ~/temp_ispvm
tar -xvzf ispvm_v17_6_linux.tar.gz 
mv isptools/ ../Lattice/ispvm/
cd ~ && rm -R ~/temp_ispvm
= Exporting environment variables = Before launching for the first time the LatticeMico32 System we have to create and export some environment variables needed to compile projects into LatticeMico32 System. Open the ~/.profile file with a text editor (i.e. Gedit) and append the following lines: 
export ISPVM_DIR=/home/user/Lattice/ispvm/isptools/ispvmsystem/
export RTDRUID_ECLIPSE_HOME=/home/user/Evidence/eclipse
export EEBASE=/home/user/Evidence/Erika/ee
export CAL_BASE=/home/user/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject
export ACTORS_JAVA=/usr/bin/java
Open a new Terminal window and export the newly created environment variables by copying the very same lines you've just added. Or, if you prefer, relog into your system. = Launch LatticeMico32 System and compile a CAL application with ERIKA Enterprise = Employing the same Terminal window used previously to export the environment variables move to the directory where LatticeMico32 System resides and launch the executable file: 
cd ~/Lattice/micosystem
./LatticeMico32Launcher
Finally compile and run a CAL application with ERIKA Enterprise following [[Tutorial: Compiling a CAL application with ERIKA Enterprise | this tutorial]]

tar xf RL8.0.00.63.43.09_linux_lm32.tar
cd ../Lattice/
../temp_lattice/RL8.0.00.63.43.09_lm32/mico32_install.csh /home/user/temp_lattice/RL8.0.00.63.43.09_lm32

mv isptools/ ../Lattice/ispvm/
cd ~ && rm -R ~/temp_ispvm

export EEBASE=/home/user/Evidence/Erika/ee
export CAL_BASE=/home/user/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject

== Introduction == This tutorial describes all the steps to follow in order to install the tools needed to compile and run projects in CAL language on a [http://www.latticesemi.com/products/intellectualproperty/ipcores/mico32/index.cfm Lattice Mico32 platform]. For a brief introduction on the CAL language have a look at [[Brief introduction to the CAL language]] The tutorial has been tested on the FPG-EYE board produced by Evidence in which we've integrated an FPGA using a Mico32 processor. The operating system chosen is an Ubuntu 10.10 maverick running on a virtual machine, anyway the installation process could be adapted to almost all other Linux releases on virtual or physical machines. == Note for Linux Users == Since it has to be used a Linux distribution please look carefully at the following warnings: # The Evidence package installation path should NOT contain directory name with spaces. e.g. use ~/Evidence. # The actorsproject package installation path should NOT contain directory name with spaces: e.g. use ~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject. # It is strongly encouraged to adopt real paths instead of using symbolic links and aliases. # Please install all the ACTORS project compilers into their default directory. For instance, given the ACTORS project repository is installed in ~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject the compilers will have to be located in ~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject/bin == Prerequisites == As a first step you have to download the ERIKA's Enterprise repository where you will find, among other things, the CAL language libraries (specifically adapted to work in Erika Enterprise), system actors created in C language and a couple of demos that can be compiled and run. Secondly install ERIKA Enterprise and RT-Druid on Linux. Both steps can be accomplished just following [[Tutorial: Installing ERIKA and RT-Druid on a Linux host]]. In the follow-up of this tutorial we will assume that you've correctly stored the ERIKA's repository in ~/Evidence/Erika and installed the eclipse_3_6_ready_to_use_LINUX_201101111314 version of ERIKA'S Enterprise under the ~/Evidence folder, in order to find the eclipse directory under ~/Evidence/eclipse Create then a virtual machine with Ubuntu 10.10 maverick as guest operating system. In our example we've used VMware Player 3.1.3 and installed WMware tools for linux version 8.4.5 version. Anyway all the tests can be smoothly deployed on a Linux physical machine. After creating the virtual machine, before proceeding with the installation process, it would be useful to completely update the packages installed in your system to the latest version. To update all the packages open a Terminal window and execute the following commands: 
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get upgrade
Now install all the packages that will be needed to compile our projects. Type: 
sudo apt-get install java-common sun-java6-bin sun-java6-jre sun-java6-jdk sun-java6-source
sudo apt-get install ant subversion csh gawk libxml2-dev libsdl1.2-dev libgtk2.0-dev
== Downloading the OpenDF repository and the ACTORS project source code == You are now ready to download the OpenDF repository on your system (i.e. in ~/opendf): 
mkdir opendf
cd opendf
svn co https://opendf.svn.sourceforge.net/svnroot/opendf/trunk
Under the OpenDF's project repository you will find all the ACTORS project source code needed for our purpose in: ~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject. Move to this directory and install the tools provided for the compilation of CAL projects by writing in a Terminal window: 
make
make install
Now you have all the tools needed to convert CAL files into C language (xlim2c compiler and others) under the directory:~/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject/bin == Installing LatticeMico32 System and ispVM System on Linux == The LatticeMico32 System is used to implement the LatticeMico32 soft microprocessor and attached peripheral components in a Lattice FPGA. It contains integrated tools that combine with ispLEVER software (which includes ispVM System) to coordinate the building of an embedded processor system on an FPGA device and write the software to drive it. All the software we will use can be downloaded from the [http://www.latticesemi.com Lattice Semiconductor site]; for our tutorial we've chosen the 8.0.00.63 version for Linux of the LatticeMico32 System and the 17.6 version for Linux of the ispVM System. Lattice Diamond doesn't work (yet) with Erika. Download the RL8.0.00.63.43.09_linux_lm32.tar file and put it on your hard disk, for instance in ~/temp_lattice. After having created in your home the ~/Lattice folder follow the steps reported below:

tar xf RL8.0.00.63.43.09_linux_lm32.tar
cd ../Lattice/
../temp_lattice/RL8.0.00.63.43.09_lm32/mico32_install.csh /home/user/temp_lattice/RL8.0.00.63.43.09_lm32
rm -R ~/temp_lattice
Accept all the terms and agreements you will be prompted. When asked, tell the setup to install both gtool and Lattice Mico32 System Tools and point out you are not installing neither from a dvd drive, nor from a cd one. Next install ispVM System on your virtual machine; put the ispvm_v17_6_linux.tar.gz file on a newly created ~/temp_ispvm directory, create the ~/Lattice/ispvm folder and follow the steps reported below: 
cd ~/temp_ispvm
tar -xvzf ispvm_v17_6_linux.tar.gz 
mv isptools/ ../Lattice/ispvm/
cd ~ && rm -R ~/temp_ispvm
== Exporting environment variables == Before launching for the first time the LatticeMico32 System we have to create and export some environment variables needed to compile projects into LatticeMico32 System. Open the ~/.profile file with a text editor (i.e. Gedit) and append the following lines: 
export ISPVM_DIR=/home/user/Lattice/ispvm/isptools/ispvmsystem/
export RTDRUID_ECLIPSE_HOME=/home/user/Evidence/eclipse
export EEBASE=/home/user/Evidence/Erika/ee
export CAL_BASE=/home/user/opendf/trunk/contrib/actorsproject
export ACTORS_JAVA=/usr/bin/java
Open a new Terminal window and export the newly created environment variables by copying the very same lines you've just added. Or, if you prefer, relog into your system. == Launch LatticeMico32 System and compile a CAL application with ERIKA Enterprise == Employing the same Terminal window used previously to export the environment variables move to the directory where LatticeMico32 System resides and launch the executable file: 
cd ~/Lattice/micosystem
./LatticeMico32Launcher
Finally compile and run a CAL application with ERIKA Enterprise following the [[Tutorial: Compiling a CAL application with ERIKA Enterprise]].

= Introduction =
This small tutorial describes the steps needed to download, compile and run a simple application showing the main features of Erika Enterprise and RT-Druid for the Microchip dsPIC DSC platform.
This tutorial has been tested on a FLEX board produced by Evidence and Embedded Solutions and on a Microchip Explorer 16 development board from Microchip.
Even if all the steps needed to run an application will be depicted, a preliminary knowledge on the Microchip MPLAB X and its debug environment should be useful to the reader.

= Introduction =
This small tutorial describes the steps needed to download, compile and run a simple application showing the main features of Erika Enterprise and RT-Druid for the Microchip dsPIC DSC platform.
This tutorial has been tested on a FLEX board produced by Evidence and Embedded Solutions and on a Microchip Explorer 16 development board from Microchip.
Even if all the steps needed to run an application will be depicted, a preliminary knowledge on the Microchip MPLAB X and its debug environment should be useful to the reader.
= Note for Windows XP and Windows Vista users =
If you are using Windows, and especially if you are using Windows Vista, please look carefully at the following warnings:
# The Evidence package installation path should NOT contain directory name with spaces. For e.g. use <tt>c:/Evidence</tt> # The Scilab package installation path should NOT contain directory name with spaces. For e.g. use <tt>c:/Evidence/scicoslab-4.4b7</tt> # If using Vista, be aware that directories like <tt>c:/Programmi</tt>, <tt>c:/Users/Documenti</tt> are not REAL directories but are aliases. DO NOT USE THEM. Put your RT-Druid workspace under <tt>c:/Users/yourusername/workspace</tt>. # Please install cygwin into its default directory, <tt>c:/cygwin</tt>. # Also if from the Windows Vista Explorer your Microchip compiler seems to be installed under <tt>c:/Programmi/Microchip/...</tt>, please remember to specify the REAL pathname. In particular, <tt>c:/Programmi</tt> '''DOES NOT EXISTS''', whereas the correct name is <tt>c:/Program Files</tt>.

#sudo apt-get update #sudo apt-get upgrade
To execute the MPLAB X IDE a java virtual machine have to be installed. Before to proceed with the JRE installation you need to check the multiverse repository enabled. You can perform this step from the Ubuntu Software Center and select "Edit -> Software Sources...", after inserting you password you must check the "Software restricetd by copiright or legal issues (multiverse)" option; otherwise you can enable this repository by editing the source.list, to do that in a Terminal window execute:
sudo gedit /etc/apt/source.list
Then on the gedit window uncomment the following lines:
deb http://it.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/ maverick universe deb-src http://it.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/ maverick universe deb http://it.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/ maverick-updates universe deb-src http://it.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/ maverick-updates universe
by removing the "#" character, save the file and close gedit.
Finally to install the JRE on a Terminal window insert:
# sudo apt-get update # sudo apt-get install sun-java6-jre sun-java6-plugin sun-java6-fonts

= Installing ERIKA Enterprise and RT-Druid on Linux =

= Introduction =
This small tutorial describes the steps needed to download, compile and run a simple application showing the main features of Erika Enterprise and RT-Druid for the Microchip dsPIC DSC platform.
This tutorial has been tested on a FLEX board produced by Evidence and Embedded Solutions and on a Microchip Explorer 16 development board from Microchip. Moreover, the needed software has been installed and tested on an Ubuntu 11.04 Natty Narwhal but the installation process should be adapted to almost all the other releases.
Even if all the steps needed to run an application will be depicted, a preliminary knowledge on the Microchip MPLAB X and its debug environment should be useful to the reader.
= Note for Linux Users =
If you are using a Linux distribution please look carefully at the following warnings:
# The Evidence package installation path should NOT contain directory name with spaces. e.g. use <tt>~/Evidence</tt>. # The Scilab package installation path should NOT contain directory name with spaces: e.g. use <tt>~/Evidence/scicoslab-4.4b7</tt>. # It is strongly encouraged the adoption of the real path instead of using symbolic links and aliases. # Please install all the Microchip compilers into their default directory (<tt>/opt/XXXX</tt>).
= Prerequisite = Before proceeding with the installation process it should be useful to completely update the packages installed in you system to the latest version. To update all the packages open a Terminal window and execute the following commands:
#sudo apt-get update #sudo apt-get upgrade
To execute the MPLAB X IDE a java virtual machine have to be installed. Before to proceed with the JRE installation you need to check the multiverse repository enabled. You can perform this step from the Ubuntu Software Center and select "Edit -> Software Sources...", after inserting you password you must check the "Software restricetd by copiright or legal issues (multiverse)" option; otherwise you can enable this repository by editing the source.list, to do that in a Terminal window execute:
sudo gedit /etc/apt/source.list
Then on the gedit window uncomment the following lines:
deb http://it.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/ maverick universe deb-src http://it.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/ maverick universe deb http://it.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/ maverick-updates universe deb-src http://it.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/ maverick-updates universe
by removing the "#" character, save the file and close gedit.
Finally to install the JRE on a Terminal window insert:
# sudo apt-get update # sudo apt-get install sun-java6-jre sun-java6-plugin sun-java6-fonts

= Introduction = This small tutorial describes the steps needed to download, compile and run a simple application showing the main features of Erika Enterprise and RT-Druid for the Microchip dsPIC DSC platform. This tutorial has been tested on a FLEX board produced by Evidence and Embedded Solutions and on a Microchip Explorer 16 development board from Microchip. Moreover, the needed software has been installed and tested on an Ubuntu 11.04 Natty Narwhal but the installation process should be adapted to almost all the other releases. Even if all the steps needed to run an application will be depicted, a preliminary knowledge on the Microchip MPLAB X and its debug environment should be useful to the reader. = Note for Linux Users = If you are using a Linux distribution please look carefully at the following warnings: # The Evidence package installation path should NOT contain directory name with spaces. e.g. use ~/Evidence. # The Scilab package installation path should NOT contain directory name with spaces: e.g. use ~/Evidence/scicoslab-4.4b7. # It is strongly encouraged the adoption of the real path instead of using symbolic links and aliases. # Please install all the Microchip compilers into their default directory (/opt/XXXX). = Prerequisites = Before proceeding with the installation process it should be useful to completely update the packages installed in you system to the latest version. To update all the packages open a Terminal window and execute the following commands: 
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get upgrade
To execute the MPLAB X IDE a 32bit JRE have to be installed. Before to proceed with the JRE installation you need to check the multiverse repository enabled. You can perform this step from the Ubuntu Software Center and select "Edit -> Software Sources...", after inserting you password you must check the "Software restricetd by copiright or legal issues (multiverse)" option; otherwise you can enable this repository by editing the source.list, to do that in a Terminal window execute: 
sudo gedit /etc/apt/source.list
Then on the gedit window uncomment the following lines: deb http://it.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/ maverick universe
deb-src http://it.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/ maverick universe
deb http://it.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/ maverick-updates universe
deb-src http://it.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/ maverick-updates universe
by removing the "#" character, then save the file and close gedit. Finally to install the JRE on a Terminal window insert: 
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install sun-java6-jre sun-java6-plugin sun-java6-fonts
Please notice that by installing a 64bit JRE RT-Druid will not work properly. = Installing MPLAB X IDE = To download the the MPLAB X IDE in a TErminal window execute: 
cd ~

mkdir mplab_temp
cd mplab_temp

wget http://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/mplab/X_Beta/mplabxidebeta32.bin
wget http://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/mplab/X_Beta/mplabc18.bin
wget http://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/mplab/X_Beta/mplabc30.bin
wget http://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/mplab/X_Beta/mplabc32.bin

chmod a+x *.bin

sudo ./mplabxidebeta32.bin
sudo ./mplabc32.bin
sudo ./mplabc30.bin
sudo ./mplabc18.bin
At the end of the installation process either the directory and the bin files can be removed: 
cd ~
rm -r mplab_temp
To enable either the correct execution of the MPLAB X IDE you must set the owner of the MPLAB X IDE 
sudo chown user:user ~/MPLAB\ X\ IDE\ beta4.desktop
please notice that "user" must be substitued with your username on the Linux host. Moreover, to enable MPLAB XIDE to connect with the supported programmers you must set the execution flag to the file dorun.sh 
sudo chmod +x /opt/microchip/mplab_ide/ide/bin/nativeexecution/dorun.sh

For furter information on MPLAB X please visit
http://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/mplab/X_Beta
 
and/or download

http://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/mplab/X_Beta/Getting_Started_with_MPLAB-X.pdf

= Introduction = This small tutorial describes the steps needed to download, compile and run a simple application showing the main features of Erika Enterprise and RT-Druid for the Microchip dsPIC DSC platform. This tutorial has been tested on a FLEX board produced by Evidence and Embedded Solutions and on a Microchip Explorer 16 development board from Microchip. Moreover, the needed software has been installed and tested on an Ubuntu 11.04 Natty Narwhal but the installation process should be adapted to almost all the other releases. Even if all the steps needed to run an application will be depicted, a preliminary knowledge on the Microchip MPLAB X and its debug environment should be useful to the reader. = Note for Linux Users = If you are using a Linux distribution please look carefully at the following warnings: # The Evidence package installation path should NOT contain directory name with spaces. e.g. use ~/Evidence. # The Scilab package installation path should NOT contain directory name with spaces: e.g. use ~/Evidence/scicoslab-4.4b7. # It is strongly encouraged the adoption of the real path instead of using symbolic links and aliases. # Please install all the Microchip compilers into their default directory (/opt/XXXX). = Prerequisites = Before proceeding with the installation process it should be useful to completely update the packages installed in you system to the latest version. To update all the packages open a Terminal window and execute the following commands: 
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get upgrade
To execute the MPLAB X IDE a 32bit JRE have to be installed. Before to proceed with the JRE installation you need to check the multiverse repository enabled. You can perform this step from the Ubuntu Software Center and select "Edit -> Software Sources...", after inserting you password you must check the "Software restricetd by copiright or legal issues (multiverse)" option; otherwise you can enable this repository by editing the source.list, to do that in a Terminal window execute: 
sudo gedit /etc/apt/sources.list
Then on the gedit window uncomment the following lines: deb http://it.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/ maverick universe
deb-src http://it.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/ maverick universe
deb http://it.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/ maverick-updates universe
deb-src http://it.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/ maverick-updates universe
by removing the "#" character, then save the file and close gedit. Finally to install the JRE on a Terminal window insert: 
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install sun-java6-jre sun-java6-plugin sun-java6-fonts
Please notice that by installing a 64bit JRE RT-Druid will not work properly. = Installing MPLAB X IDE = To download the the MPLAB X IDE in a TErminal window execute: 
cd ~

mkdir mplab_temp
cd mplab_temp

wget http://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/mplab/X_Beta/mplabc18.bin

wget http://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/mplab/X_Beta/mplabc32.bin

chmod a+x *.bin

sudo ./mplabxidebeta32.bin
sudo ./mplabc32.bin
sudo ./mplabc30.bin
sudo ./mplabc18.bin
At the end of the installation process either the directory and the bin files can be removed: 
cd ~
rm -r mplab_temp
To enable either the correct execution of the MPLAB X IDE you must set the owner of the MPLAB X IDE 
sudo chown user:user ~/MPLAB\ X\ IDE\ beta4.desktop
please notice that "user" must be substitued with your username on the Linux host. Moreover, to enable MPLAB XIDE to connect with the supported programmers you must set the execution flag to the file dorun.sh 
sudo chmod +x /opt/microchip/mplab_ide/ide/bin/nativeexecution/dorun.sh
For furter information on MPLAB X please visit
http://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/mplab/X_Beta

= Introduction = This small tutorial describes the steps needed to download, compile and run a simple application showing the main features of Erika Enterprise and RT-Druid for the Microchip dsPIC DSC platform. This tutorial has been tested on a FLEX board produced by Evidence and Embedded Solutions and on a Microchip Explorer 16 development board from Microchip. Moreover, the needed software has been installed and tested on an Ubuntu 11.04 Natty Narwhal but the installation process should be adapted to almost all the other releases. Even if all the steps needed to run an application will be depicted, a preliminary knowledge on the Microchip MPLAB X and its debug environment should be useful to the reader. = Note for Linux Users = If you are using a Linux distribution please look carefully at the following warnings: # The Evidence package installation path should NOT contain directory name with spaces. e.g. use ~/Evidence. # The Scilab package installation path should NOT contain directory name with spaces: e.g. use ~/Evidence/scicoslab-4.4b7. # It is strongly encouraged the adoption of the real path instead of using symbolic links and aliases. # Please install all the Microchip compilers into their default directory (/opt/XXXX). = Prerequisites = Before proceeding with the installation process it should be useful to completely update the packages installed in you system to the latest version. To update all the packages open a Terminal window and execute the following commands: 
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get upgrade
To execute the MPLAB X IDE a 32bit JRE have to be installed. Before to proceed with the JRE installation you need to check the multiverse repository enabled. You can perform this step from the Ubuntu Software Center and select "Edit -> Software Sources...", after inserting you password you must check the "Software restricetd by copiright or legal issues (multiverse)" option; otherwise you can enable this repository by editing the source.list, to do that in a Terminal window execute: 
sudo gedit /etc/apt/sources.list

by removing the "#" character, then save the file and close gedit. Finally to install the JRE on a Terminal window insert: 
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install sun-java6-jre sun-java6-plugin sun-java6-fonts
Please notice that by installing a 64bit JRE RT-Druid will not work properly. = Installing MPLAB X IDE = To download the the MPLAB X IDE in a TErminal window execute:

cd mplab_temp

rm -r mplab_temp

This tutorial has been tested on a FLEX board produced by Evidence and Embedded Solutions and on a Microchip Explorer 16 development board from Microchip. Moreover, the needed software has been installed and tested on an Ubuntu 11.04 Natty Narwhal but the installation process should be adapted to almost all the other releases. Even if all the steps needed to run an application will be depicted, a preliminary knowledge on the Microchip MPLAB X and its debug environment should be useful to the reader. = Note for Linux Users = If you are using a Linux distribution please look carefully at the following warnings: # The Evidence package installation path should NOT contain directory name with spaces. e.g. use ~/Evidence. # The Scilab package installation path should NOT contain directory name with spaces: e.g. use ~/Evidence/scicoslab-4.4b7. # It is strongly encouraged the adoption of the real path instead of using symbolic links and aliases. # Please install all the Microchip compilers into their default directory (/opt/XXXX). = Prerequisites = Before proceeding with the installation process it should be useful to completely update the packages installed in you system to the latest version. To update all the packages open a Terminal window and execute the following commands: 
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get upgrade
To execute the MPLAB X IDE a 32bit JRE have to be installed. Before to proceed with the JRE installation you need to check the multiverse repository enabled. You can perform this step from the Ubuntu Software Center and select "Edit -> Software Sources...", after inserting you password you must check the "Software restricetd by copiright or legal issues (multiverse)" option; otherwise you can enable this repository by editing the source.list, to do that in a Terminal window execute: 
sudo gedit /etc/apt/sources.list
Then on the gedit window uncomment the line: deb http://archive.canonical.com/ubuntu maverick partner
by removing the "#" character, then save the file and close gedit. Finally to install the JRE on a Terminal window insert: 
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install sun-java6-jre sun-java6-plugin sun-java6-fonts
Please notice that by installing a 64bit JRE RT-Druid will not work properly. = Installing MPLAB X IDE = To download the the MPLAB X IDE in a Terminal window execute: 
cd ~

mkdir mplab_temp
cd mplab_temp

wget http://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/mplab/X_Beta/mplabxidebeta32.bin
wget http://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/mplab/X_Beta/mplabc18.bin
wget http://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/mplab/X_Beta/mplabc30.bin
wget http://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/mplab/X_Beta/mplabc32.bin

chmod a+x *.bin

sudo ./mplabxidebeta32.bin
sudo ./mplabc32.bin
sudo ./mplabc30.bin
sudo ./mplabc18.bin
Please notice that this step can require few minutes depending on the downloading speed.
You can speedup this process by downloading and installing only the compiles needed by your platform. Please remember to reboot you system after the installation of the last compiler. At the end of the installation process either the directory and the bin files can be removed: 
cd ~
rm -r mplab_temp
To enable the correct execution of the MPLAB X IDE you must set the owner of the MPLAB X IDE 
sudo chown user:user ~/Desktop/MPLAB\ X\ IDE\ beta4.desktop
please notice that "user" must be substitued with your username on the Linux host. Moreover, the location of the file depends on the language of your installed OS, e.g. for italian people the file could be located on ~/Scrivania/MPLAB\ X\ IDE\ beta4.desktop. Moreover, to enable MPLAB X IDE to connect with the supported programmers you must set the execution flag to the file dorun.sh 
sudo chmod +x /opt/microchip/mplab_ide/ide/bin/nativeexecution/dorun.sh
For furter information on MPLAB X IDE and its supported programmers please visit
http://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/mplab/X_Beta
and/or download
http://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/mplab/X_Beta/Getting_Started_with_MPLAB-X.pdf = Installing ERIKA Enterprise and RT-Druid on Linux = = First RT-Druid startup and configuration = To download RT-Druid you can select the correct file from the webpage:
http://erika.tuxfamily.org/erika-for-multiple-devices/betaversionerikaenterprisertdruid160.html
or simply insert in a Terminal window 
cd ~
mkdir eclipse_temp
cd eclipse_temp

wget http://download.tuxfamily.org/erika/webdownload/rtdruid_eclipse37/eclipse_3_7_ready_to_use_LINUX.zip
Please notice that the download process can require few minutes depending on the downloading speed. = Compiling your first ERIKA Enterprise demo = = Running your first ERIKA Enterprise demo =

wget http://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/mplab/X_Beta/mplabc18.bin
wget http://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/mplab/X_Beta/mplabc30.bin
wget http://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/mplab/X_Beta/mplabc32.bin

chmod a+x *.bin

sudo ./mplabxidebeta32.bin
sudo ./mplabc32.bin
sudo ./mplabc30.bin
sudo ./mplabc18.bin
Please notice that this step can require few minutes depending on the downloading speed.
You can speedup this process by downloading and installing only the compiles needed by your platform. Please remember to reboot you system after the installation of the last compiler. At the end of the installation process either the directory and the bin files can be removed:

rm -r mplab_temp
To enable the correct execution of the MPLAB X IDE you must set the owner of the MPLAB X IDE

For furter information on MPLAB X IDE and its supported programmers please visit

To enable the updates of RT-Driud and its related distribution of Erika Enterprise XXXXXX http://download.tuxfamily.org/erika/webdownload/rtdruid_beta Please unselect the option "Contact all site during install to find required software" to speed up update process. sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get upgrade

sudo gedit /etc/apt/sources.list
Then on the gedit window uncomment the line: deb http://archive.canonical.com/ubuntu maverick partner
by removing the "#" character, then save the file and close gedit. Finally to install the JRE on a Terminal window insert: 
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install sun-java6-jre sun-java6-plugin sun-java6-fonts
Please notice that by installing a 64bit JRE RT-Druid will not work properly. = Installing MPLAB X IDE = To download the the MPLAB X IDE in a Terminal window execute: 
cd ~

mkdir mplab_temp
cd mplab_temp

please notice that "user" must be substitued with your username on the Linux host. Moreover, the location of the file depends on the language of your installed OS, e.g. for italian people the file could be located on ~/Scrivania/MPLAB\ X\ IDE\ beta4.desktop. For furter information on MPLAB X IDE and its supported programmers please visit

To enable the updates of RT-Driud and its related distribution of Erika Enterprise XXXXXX http://download.tuxfamily.org/erika/webdownload/rtdruid_beta Please unselect the option "Contact all site during install to find required software" to speed up update process.
